title.zh: 卷四百十八 列傳第一百七十七 吳潛 程元鳳 江萬里 王爚 章鑑 陳宜中 文天祥
title.en: Volume 418 Biographies 177: Wu Qian, Cheng Yuanfeng, Jiang Wanli, Wang Yue, Zhang Jian, Chen Yizhong, Wen Tianxiang
title.raw: 卷四百十八 列傳第一百七十七 吳潛 程元鳳 江萬里 王爚 章鑑 陳宜中 文天祥 Volume 418 Biographies 177: Wu Qian, Cheng Yuanfeng, Jiang Wanli, Wang Yue, Zhang Jian, Chen Yizhong, Wen Tianxiang

sentences.zh: 吳潛 程元鳳 江萬里 王爚 章鑒 陳宜中 文天祥

translations.literal: Wu Qian, Cheng Yuanfeng, Jiang Wanli, Wang Yue, Zhang Jian, Chen Yizhong, Wen Tianxiang
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qian, Cheng Yuanfeng, Jiang Wanli, Wang Yue, Zhang Jian, Chen Yizhong, and Wen Tianxiang

sentences.zh: 吳潛，字毅夫，宣州寧國人。

translations.literal: Wu Qian, courtesy name Yifu, was a native of Ningguo in Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qian, whose courtesy name was Yifu, came from Ningguo in Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 秘閣修撰柔勝之季子。

translations.literal: He was the youngest son of Rou Sheng, Compiler at the Secretariat Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was the youngest son of Rou Sheng, who held the post of Secretariat Pavilion compiler.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十年進士第一，授承事郎、簽鎮東軍節度判官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiading he ranked first among jinshi graduates and was appointed Gentleman for Progressive Service and signing secretary to the military governor of Zhendong.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the jinshi examinations in the tenth year of the Jiading reign and was appointed Gentleman for Progressive Service and signing secretary to the Zhendong military commission.

sentences.zh: 改簽廣德軍判官。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as signing secretary to the Guangde military commission.
translations.idiomatic: His appointment was changed to signing secretary for the Guangde command.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，服除，授秘書省正字，遷校書郎，添差通判嘉興府，權發遣嘉興府事。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he observed mourning; when the mourning ended he was appointed Corrector in the Secretariat, promoted to Proofreader, given an additional assignment as vice-prefect of Jiaxing, and authorized to handle Jiaxing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After observing mourning for his father, he was appointed a corrector in the Secretariat, promoted to proofreader, given an additional post as vice-prefect of Jiaxing, and entrusted with the administration of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 轉朝散郎、尚書金部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman for Dispersing the Dawn and Vice Director of the Revenue Section in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman for Dispersing the Dawn and made vice director of the revenue section in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 紹定四年，遷尚右郎官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoding he was promoted to Director of the Right Section in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Shaoding reign he was promoted to director of the right section in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 都城大火，潛上疏論致災之由：「願陛下齋戒修省，恐懼對越，菲衣惡食，必使國人信之，毋徒減膳而已。

translations.literal: When a great fire struck the capital, Qian submitted a memorial on the causes of the calamity: "I hope Your Majesty will fast, purify yourself, and cultivate self-examination, approach Heaven with fear and reverence, wear coarse clothes and eat plain food, and make the people truly believe it—not merely reduce the imperial meals.
translations.idiomatic: When a great fire broke out in the capital, Qian memorialized the throne on why disaster had come, pleading: "May Your Majesty fast, examine your conduct, and approach Heaven with awe; wear plain clothes and eat simple fare until the people truly believe you—and not merely cut back the imperial table.

sentences.zh: 疏損聲色，必使天下孚之，毋徒徹樂而已。

translations.literal: Reduce music and sensual pleasures so that all under Heaven truly trusts you—not merely withdraw musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Cut back music and sensual indulgence until the empire is genuinely convinced—not merely dismiss the court musicians.

sentences.zh: 閹官之竊弄威福者勿親，女寵之根萌禍患者勿昵。

translations.literal: Do not be intimate with eunuchs who usurp authority and blessings; do not dote on favored women in whom the roots of calamity are sprouting.
translations.idiomatic: Keep your distance from eunuchs who seize power for themselves, and from favored consorts in whom the seeds of disaster are already growing.

sentences.zh: 以暗室屋漏為尊嚴之區，而必敬必戒，以恆舞酣歌為亂亡之宅，而不淫不泆。

translations.literal: Treat the hidden chamber and the roof beam as places of dignity, always reverent and cautious; regard constant dancing and drunken song as dwellings of disorder and ruin, and be neither licentious nor dissolute.
translations.idiomatic: Hold even the innermost room sacred and remain ever reverent and watchful; treat ceaseless revelry as the road to ruin, and keep yourself from excess and dissipation.

sentences.zh: 使皇天后土知陛下有畏之之心，使三軍百姓知陛下有憂之之心。

translations.literal: Let Heaven and Earth know that Your Majesty has a heart of awe; let the armies and the people know that Your Majesty has a heart of concern.
translations.idiomatic: Let Heaven and Earth see that you stand in awe of them, and let soldiers and commoners alike see that you truly grieve for the realm.

sentences.zh: 然後，明詔二三大臣，和衷竭慮，力改弦轍，收召賢哲，選用忠良。

translations.literal: Then clearly command the chief ministers to unite their hearts and exhaust their thoughts, vigorously change course, summon the worthy and wise, and select the loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: Then issue a clear edict to your leading ministers to work in concert, change policy decisively, recall men of talent, and appoint the loyal and capable.

sentences.zh: 貪殘者屏，回邪者斥，懷奸黨賊者誅，賈怨誤國者黜。

translations.literal: Remove the greedy and cruel, expel the perverse and wicked, execute those who harbor treachery and band with villains, and dismiss those who trade in resentment and harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: Banish the greedy and cruel, drive out the corrupt, put to death those who plot treason, and dismiss those who stir resentment and mislead the state.

sentences.zh: 毋併進君子、小人以為包荒，毋兼容邪說、正論以為皇極，以培國家一線之脈，以救生民一旦之命。

translations.literal: Do not advance gentlemen and petty men together under the name of tolerant magnanimity; do not embrace heterodox doctrines and upright discourse alike under the name of the supreme norm—so as to nurture the state's single thread of life and save the people's momentary existence.
translations.idiomatic: Do not promote gentlemen and scoundrels side by side in the name of tolerance, nor treat heterodoxy and sound doctrine as equally valid in the name of balance—so that the dynasty's last slender lifeline may be preserved and the people rescued while there is still time.

sentences.zh: 庶幾天意可回，天災可息，弭災為祥，易亂為治。」

translations.literal: Then perhaps Heaven's intent may turn, heavenly calamities may cease, disasters may be transformed into blessings, and disorder may be changed into order."
translations.idiomatic: Only then may Heaven's wrath be turned aside, disaster abated, misfortune made into blessing, and chaos restored to order."

sentences.zh: 又言：「重地要區，當豫畜人才以備患。

translations.literal: He also said: "In important regions and strategic areas, talent should be stored up in advance against trouble.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that in vital strategic regions the court should cultivate talent in advance to meet coming crises.

sentences.zh: 論大順之理，貫通天人，當以此為致治之本。」

translations.literal: In discussing the principle of great accord, which links Heaven and man, this should be taken as the foundation of bringing order."
translations.idiomatic: On the principle of great harmony linking Heaven and humanity, he held that this should be the foundation of good government.

sentences.zh: 又貽書丞相史彌遠論事：一曰格君心，二曰節奉給，三曰振恤都民，四曰用老成廉潔之人，五曰用良將以御外患，六曰革吏弊以新治道。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to the chief councilor Shi Miyuan on affairs of state: first, rectify the ruler's mind; second, restrain court expenditures; third, relieve and succor the capital's people; fourth, employ seasoned and incorrupt men; fifth, employ good generals to meet external threats; sixth, reform bureaucratic abuses to renew the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Chief Councilor Shi Miyuan with six proposals: reform the emperor's mind; curb court spending; relieve the people of the capital; appoint seasoned and honest officials; appoint capable generals against foreign threats; and root out bureaucratic abuse to renew governance.

sentences.zh: 授直寶章閣、浙東提舉常平，辭不赴。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Attendant at the Baozhang Pavilion and Commissioner for Ever-Normal Granaries in eastern Zhejiang, but declined and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed direct attendant at the Baozhang Pavilion and granary commissioner for eastern Zhejiang, but declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 改吏部員外郎兼國史編修、實錄檢討，遷太府少卿、淮西總領。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently Compiler of the National History and Examiner of the Veritable Records, then promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Storehouse and Overall Commander for Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, with concurrent duties compiling the national history and examining the veritable records, then promoted to vice director of the palace storehouse and overall commander for Huai West.

sentences.zh: 又告執政，論用兵復河南不可輕易，以為：「金人既滅，與北為鄰，法當以和為形，以守為實，以戰為應。

translations.literal: He again informed the chief ministers that using troops to recover Henan should not be undertaken lightly, holding that: "Now that the Jurchens are destroyed and we border the north, by rule we should take peace as our form, defense as our substance, and war as our response.
translations.idiomatic: He again warned the chief ministers against rashly sending armies to recover Henan, arguing that with the Jin gone and the northern foe on the border, the state should present a face of peace, rely on defense in substance, and resort to war only when necessary.

sentences.zh: 自荊襄首納空城，合兵攻蔡，兵事一開，調度浸廣，百姓狼狽，死者枕藉，使生靈肝腦塗地，得城不過荊榛之區，獲俘不過暖昧之骨，而吾之內地荼毒如此，邊臣誤國之罪，不待言矣。

translations.literal: Since Jing and Xiang first surrendered empty cities and combined forces to attack Cai, once war began supplies and levies grew ever broader, the people were thrown into disorder, and the dead lay piled one upon another, so that living souls had their livers and brains smeared on the ground; cities taken were no more than tracts of thorns and brambles, captives taken no more than dubious bones—while our interior was ravaged thus; the border officials' crime of misleading the state needs no further words.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jing and Xiang had yielded empty cities and troops were massed against Cai, the opening of hostilities swelled levies and logistics beyond control; the people were driven to desperation and the dead lay in heaps, their lives wasted for gains no better than wasteland and doubtful spoils—while the heartland was poisoned thus. The frontier ministers' guilt in misleading the state scarcely needs stating.

sentences.zh: 聞有進恢復之畫者，其算可謂俊傑，然取之若易，守之實難。

translations.literal: I hear there are those who advance plans for recovery; their schemes may be called brilliant, yet taking territory seems easy while holding it is truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: I hear men proposing plans of reconquest whose strategy seems brilliant, yet what looks easy to seize proves hard to hold.

sentences.zh: 征行之具，何所取資，民窮不堪，激而為變，內郡率為盜賊矣。

translations.literal: With what resources are the means for campaigning to be obtained? The people, driven to destitution, will be provoked into revolt, and the interior prefectures will largely become bandit country.
translations.idiomatic: Where are the supplies for such campaigns to come from? The people, already at breaking point, will rise in revolt, and the interior prefectures will turn to banditry.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，豈容輕議。」

translations.literal: Matters of today—how can they be lightly debated?"
translations.idiomatic: The situation today brooks no rash counsel.

sentences.zh: 自後，興師入洛，潰敗失亡不貲，潛之言率驗。

translations.literal: Thereafter troops were raised and entered Luoyang; they were routed and losses were beyond reckoning—and Qian's words were largely borne out.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the court raised armies into Luoyang; they were routed and losses were incalculable—and Qian's warnings proved largely true.

sentences.zh: 遷太府卿兼權沿江制置、知建康府、江東安撫留守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Palace Storehouse, concurrently acting Commissioner for Defense along the Yangzi, Prefect of Jiankang, and Pacification Commissioner and Military Governor of Jiang East.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the palace storehouse, with concurrent authority as Yangzi defense commissioner, prefect of Jiankang, and pacification commissioner and military governor of Jiang East.

sentences.zh: 上疏論保蜀之方，護襄之策，防江之算，備海之宜，進取有甚難者三事。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on methods to preserve Shu, strategies to protect Xiang, calculations for defending the Yangzi, and measures for securing the sea coast, and on three matters in which advance was especially difficult.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on how to hold Shu, protect Xiangyang, defend the Yangzi line, and secure the coast, and on three points where offensive action would be especially perilous.

sentences.zh: 進右文殿修撰、集英殿修撰、樞密都承旨、督府參謀官兼知太平州，五辭不允。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Compiler at the Youwen Hall and the Jiying Hall, Chief Secretariat Attendant at the Bureau of Military Affairs, Staff Officer at the Command Headquarters, and concurrently Prefect of Taiping; he declined five times but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to compiler at the Youwen and Jiying halls, chief attendant at the Bureau of Military Affairs, and staff officer at headquarters with concurrent prefecture of Taiping; he declined five times but the court would not accept his refusal.

sentences.zh: 又言和戰成敗大計，宜急救襄陽等事。

translations.literal: He again spoke on the great plan of success or failure in peace and war, and that Xiangyang and the like should urgently be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: He again urged the grand strategy of peace and war and called for urgent relief of Xiangyang and related posts.

sentences.zh: 貽書執政，論京西既失，當招收京淮丁壯為精兵，以保江西。

translations.literal: He sent a letter to the chief ministers, arguing that since western Jing was lost, able-bodied men of Jing and Huai should be recruited as crack troops to secure Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the chief ministers that with western Jing lost, the court should recruit able men from the Jing and Huai regions as elite troops to hold Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 權工部侍郎、知江州，辭不赴。

translations.literal: He was given acting appointment as Vice Minister of Works and Prefect of Jiangzhou, but declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting vice minister of works and prefect of Jiangzhou, but declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 請養宗子以系國本，以鎮人心。

translations.literal: He requested that an imperial clansman be raised to secure the foundation of the state and steady popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that a member of the imperial clan be designated heir to shore up the succession and calm the people's minds.

sentences.zh: 改權兵部侍郎兼檢正。

translations.literal: He was changed to acting Vice Minister of War, concurrently Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as acting vice minister of war with concurrent duties as rectifier.

sentences.zh: 論士大夫私意之敝，以為：「襄、漢潰決，興、沔破亡，兩淮俶擾，三川陷沒。

translations.literal: He discussed the harm of private motives among scholar-officials, holding that: "Xiang and Han have burst their banks, Xing and Mian have fallen, the two Huai regions are in turmoil, and the Three Gorges region is lost.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke on how private faction among the literati had ruined policy, saying: "Xiang and Han have collapsed, Xing and Mian are lost, the two Huai regions are in turmoil, and Sichuan has fallen.

sentences.zh: 慾望陛下念大業將傾，士習已壞，以靜專察群情，以剛明消眾慝，警於有位，各勵至公。

translations.literal: I desire that Your Majesty reflect that the great enterprise is about to topple and official custom is already corrupt; with calm concentration observe the feelings of the multitude, with firm clarity dispel the many evils, warn those in office, and each encourage utmost public spirit.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to see that the great enterprise is tottering and official morals are rotten: observe the mood of the realm with calm attention, cut through popular evils with firm clarity, and warn every officeholder to strive for the public good alone.

sentences.zh: 毋以術數相高，而以事功相勉；

translations.literal: Do not vie with one another in occult arts and numerology, but encourage one another in real achievement;
translations.idiomatic: Do not compete in divination and occult arts, but spur one another to real achievement;

sentences.zh: 毋以陰謀相訐，而以識見相先。

translations.literal: do not denounce one another with secret plots, but take the lead with insight and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: do not undercut one another with secret intrigues, but lead with sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 協謀並智，戮力一心，則危者尚可安，而衰證尚可起也。」

translations.literal: Unite counsel and combine wisdom, join strength with one heart—then what is perilous may still be made secure, and declining signs may still be reversed."
translations.idiomatic: Pool counsel and act as one, and what is perilous may yet be stabilized and what is failing may yet be revived."

sentences.zh: 又請分路取士，以收淮、襄之人物。

translations.literal: He also requested that civil-service candidates be selected by circuit, so as to gather talent from Huai and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that examinations be held by circuit to recruit men of talent from the Huai and Xiang regions.

sentences.zh: 試工部侍郎、知慶元府兼沿海制置使，改知平江府，條具財計凋敝本末，以寬郡民，與轉運使王野爭論利害。

translations.literal: He was tried out as Vice Minister of Works, Prefect of Qingyuan, and concurrently Coastal Defense Commissioner; he was changed to Prefect of Pingjiang, set forth in detail the causes and course of fiscal exhaustion, to ease the burden on the prefecture's people, and debated gains and losses with Transport Commissioner Wang Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice minister of works and prefect of Qingyuan with concurrent coastal defense duties, then was transferred to Pingjiang, where he laid out the full story of fiscal collapse to relieve the people and disputed policy with transport commissioner Wang Ye.

sentences.zh: 授寶謨閣待制，提舉太平興國宮，改玉隆萬壽宮。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Gentleman at the Baomo Pavilion and Superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace, then changed to the Yulong Wanshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attendant gentleman at the Baomo Pavilion and superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace, later transferred to the Yulong Wanshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 試戶部侍郎、淮東總領兼知鎮江府。

translations.literal: He was tried out as Vice Minister of Revenue, Overall Commander for Huai East, and concurrently Prefect of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice minister of revenue, overall commander for Huai East, and concurrent prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 言邊儲防禦等十有五事。

translations.literal: He spoke on fifteen matters concerning frontier stores and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted fifteen proposals on frontier supplies and defense.

sentences.zh: 改寶謨閣直學士，兼浙西都大提點坑冶，權兵部尚書、浙西制置使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Academician of the Baomo Pavilion, concurrently Grand Commissioner for Mining in western Zhejiang, acting Minister of War, and Commissioner for Defense in western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician of the Baomo Pavilion, with concurrent charge of mining in western Zhejiang, acting minister of war, and defense commissioner for western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 申論防拓江海，團結措置等事。

translations.literal: He submitted arguments on defending and securing the rivers and sea, organizing and arranging measures, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on coastal and river defense and on organizing local resistance.

sentences.zh: 進工部尚書，改吏部尚書兼知臨安府，乃論艱屯蹇困之時，非反身修德，無以求亨通之理。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Minister of Works, then changed to Minister of Personnel and concurrently Prefect of Lin'an; he then argued that in times of hardship and distress, unless one turns inward and cultivates virtue, there is no way to seek the principle of flourishing success.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of works, then made minister of personnel and concurrent prefect of Lin'an, where he argued that in such desperate times only moral self-reform could restore the state's fortunes.

sentences.zh: 乞遴選近族以系人望，而俟太子之生。

translations.literal: He begged that a near kinsman of the imperial house be selected to secure popular expectation, while awaiting the birth of a crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that a close imperial kinsman be chosen to satisfy public expectation until a crown prince should be born.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 兼侍讀經筵，以台臣徐榮叟論列，授寶謨閣學士、知紹興府、浙東安撫使，辭，提舉南京鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: Concurrently Lecturer at the Classics Colloquium; because Censor Xu Rongsou impeached him, he was appointed Academician of the Baomo Pavilion, Prefect of Shaoxing, and Pacification Commissioner of eastern Zhejiang, but declined and was made Superintendent of the Hongqing Palace at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as lecturer at the classics colloquium, censor Xu Rongsou impeached him; he was appointed academician of the Baomo Pavilion and prefect and pacification commissioner of Shaoxing, declined, and was made superintendent of the Hongqing Palace at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 遂請致仕，授華文閣學士知建寧府，辭。

translations.literal: He then requested retirement; he was appointed Academician of the Huawen Pavilion and Prefect of Jianning, but declined.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to retire; the court named him academician of the Huawen Pavilion and prefect of Jianning, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，服除，轉中大夫、試兵部尚書兼侍讀，轉翰林學士、知制誥兼侍讀，改端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事，進封金陵郡侯。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he observed mourning; when mourning ended he was transferred to Grandee of the Palace, tried out as Minister of War with concurrent Lecturer, then transferred to Hanlin Academician, Drafter of Edicts with concurrent Lecturer, changed to Academician of the Duanming Hall and Junior Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis of Jinling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he was made grandee of the palace and acting minister of war with concurrent lectureship, then hanlin academician and edict drafter with concurrent lectureship, then academician of the Duanming Hall and junior signatory at the Bureau of Military Affairs, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 以亢旱乞罷，免，改資政殿學士、提舉洞霄宮，改知福州兼本路安撫使。

translations.literal: Because of severe drought he begged to be dismissed and was relieved; he was changed to Academician of the Zizheng Hall and Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace, then changed to Prefect of Fuzhou with concurrent Pacification Commissioner of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Citing severe drought he asked to leave office and was dismissed, then made academician of the Zizheng Hall and superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace, and later prefect of Fuzhou with concurrent pacification commissioner of that circuit.

sentences.zh: 徙知紹興府、浙東安撫使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Shaoxing and Pacification Commissioner of eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Shaoxing and pacification commissioner of eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 召同知樞密院兼參知政事。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 入對，言：「國家之不能無敝，猶人之不能無病。

translations.literal: On entering audience he said: "That the state cannot be without decline is like a person who cannot be without illness.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he said: "A state cannot be free of decline any more than a person can be free of illness.

sentences.zh: 今日之病，不但倉、扁望之而驚，庸醫亦望而驚矣。

translations.literal: Today's illness would alarm not only Cang Gong and Bian Que on seeing it—even common physicians would be alarmed on seeing it.
translations.idiomatic: Today's malady would alarm not only the great physicians Cang Gong and Bian Que—even a common doctor would shrink from it.

sentences.zh: 願陛下篤任元老，以為醫師，博採眾益，以為醫工。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will earnestly entrust elder statesmen as chief physicians and broadly gather many benefits as medical assistants.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty deeply trust elder statesmen as your chief physicians and draw widely on many able men as their assistants.

sentences.zh: 使臣輩得以效牛溲馬勃之助，以不辱陛下知人之明。」

translations.literal: Let your servants be able to offer the humble aid of ox dung and horse bolus, so as not to dishonor Your Majesty's discernment in knowing men."
translations.idiomatic: Let us your servants contribute whatever humble aid we can, so as not to betray Your Majesty's judgment in appointing us."

sentences.zh: 淳祐十一年，入為參知政事，拜右丞相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chunyou he entered office as Vice Grand Councilor and was appointed Right Grand Councilor, concurrently Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Chunyou he became vice grand councilor and was appointed right grand councilor with concurrent command of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，以水災乞解機政。

translations.literal: The next year, because of flood disaster he begged to be relieved of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he asked to resign from the councilorship, citing flood damage.

sentences.zh: 以觀文殿大學士、提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Academician of the Guanwen Hall and Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand academician of the Guanwen Hall and superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 又四年，授沿海制置大使，判慶元府。

translations.literal: Four years later he was appointed Grand Commissioner for Coastal Defense and given charge of Qingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he was appointed grand coastal defense commissioner with jurisdiction over Qingyuan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至官，條具軍民久遠之計，告於政府，奏皆行之。

translations.literal: On reaching his post he set forth in detail long-term plans for army and people, reported them to the government, and all his memorials were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he laid out long-term plans for military and civilian affairs; the court adopted every proposal he submitted.

sentences.zh: 又積錢百四十七萬三千八百有奇，代民輸帛，前後所蠲五百四十九萬一千七百有奇。

translations.literal: He also accumulated 1,473,800-odd strings of cash to pay silk levies on the people's behalf; in all, before and after, he remitted 5,491,700-odd.
translations.idiomatic: He also amassed more than 1,473,800 strings of cash to pay the people's silk levies for them, and in all remitted more than 5,491,700 in taxes and dues.

sentences.zh: 以久任丐祠，且累章乞歸田裡，進封崇國公，判寧國府。

translations.literal: Because of long service he begged for a temple sinecure, and repeatedly memorialized to return to his home fields; he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Chong and given charge of Ningguo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After long service he sought a temple appointment and repeatedly asked to retire home; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Chong and given charge of Ningguo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 還家，以醴泉觀使兼侍讀，召入對，論畏天命，結民心，進賢才，通下情。

translations.literal: Returning home, he was made Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey with concurrent Lecturer; summoned to audience, he discussed revering Heaven's mandate, binding popular hearts, advancing worthy talent, and communicating the feelings below.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he was made commissioner of the Liquan Abbey with concurrent lectureship, then recalled to audience to speak on revering Heaven's mandate, winning the people's hearts, promoting talent, and heeding popular grievances.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his advice.

sentences.zh: 拜特進、左丞相，進封慶國公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Special Advancement and Left Grand Councilor, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed special advancement and left grand councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Qing.

sentences.zh: 奏：「乞令在朝之臣各陳所見，以決處置之宜。」

translations.literal: He memorialized: "I beg that court officials each state their views, so that the proper course of action may be decided."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, asking that every official at court state his views so the proper course of action could be decided.

sentences.zh: 改封許國公。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: His title was changed to Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 大元兵渡江攻鄂州，別將由大理下交址，破廣西、湖南諸郡。

translations.literal: Great Yuan troops crossed the Yangzi to attack Ezhou; another force descended from Dali through Jiaozhi and broke the prefectures of Guangxi and Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan forces crossed the Yangzi to attack Ezhou while another column came down from Dali through Jiaozhi and overran prefectures in Guangxi and Hunan.

sentences.zh: 潛奏：「今鄂渚被兵，湖南擾動，推原禍根，良由近年奸臣憸士設為虛議，迷國誤軍，其禍一二年而愈酷。

translations.literal: Qian memorialized: "Now the E region is under attack and Hunan is in turmoil; tracing the root of the calamity, it truly stems from treacherous ministers and crafty scholars in recent years who set up empty debates, misled the state and misled the armies—the harm growing fiercer year by year.
translations.idiomatic: Qian memorialized: "Ezhou is under attack and Hunan is in turmoil. The root of this disaster lies in the treacherous ministers and sycophants of recent years whose empty talk has misled the state and the armies—year by year the harm has grown worse.

sentences.zh: 附和逢迎，媕阿諂媚，積至於大不靖。

translations.literal: Echoing and currying favor, fawning and flattering, it accumulated until there was great unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Echoing power, fawning and flattering, they brought the realm to this pass of grave disorder.

sentences.zh: 臣年將七十，捐軀致命，所不敢辭。

translations.literal: Your servant is nearly seventy; to give his body and life he dares not decline.
translations.idiomatic: I am nearly seventy, yet I do not shrink from offering my life for the state.

sentences.zh: 所深痛者，臣交任之日，上流之兵已逾黃、漢，廣右之兵已蹈賓、柳，謂臣壞天下之事，亦可哀已。」

translations.literal: What pains me deeply is that on the day your servant took office, upstream troops had already crossed the Huang and Han, and troops in the far south had already trodden Bin and Liu—to say your servant has ruined the affairs of all under Heaven is pitiable indeed."
translations.idiomatic: What grieves me most is that on the very day I took office, the enemy had already crossed the Huang and Han in the upper Yangzi and overrun Bin and Liu in the far south—to blame me for ruining the empire is pitiful indeed."

sentences.zh: 又論國家安危治亂之原：「蓋自近年公道晦蝕，私意橫流，仁賢空虛，名節喪敗，忠嘉絕響，諛佞成風，天怒而陛下不知，人怨而陛下不察，稔成兵戈之禍，積為宗社之憂。

translations.literal: He again discussed the origins of the state's security and peril, order and disorder: "From recent years public principle has been eclipsed and private motives have flowed unchecked; benevolence and worth stand empty, reputation and integrity are lost, loyal and excellent counsel has ceased to be heard, and flattery has become the fashion—Heaven is angry yet Your Majesty does not know it, the people resent yet Your Majesty does not perceive it; war has ripened into calamity and accumulated into anxiety for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: He again traced the roots of the state's peril: "In recent years public principle has been eclipsed and private interest has run wild; the worthy stand ignored, integrity is ruined, loyal counsel is silenced, and flattery prevails—Heaven is angry yet Your Majesty does not see it, the people resent yet Your Majesty does not hear it; thus war has ripened and the altars of the dynasty are in peril.

sentences.zh: 章鑒、高鑄嘗與丁大全同官，傾心附麗，躐躋要途。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian and Gao Zhu once served in the same office as Ding Daquan; they devoted their hearts to attaching themselves to him and leapt over others into key posts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian and Gao Zhu once served with Ding Daquan, attached themselves to him, and vaulted into high office.

sentences.zh: 蕭泰來等群小噂沓，國事日非，浸淫至於今日。

translations.literal: Petty men such as Xiao Tailai slandered and clamored; state affairs daily worsened, seeping until today.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men like Xiao Tailai spread slander while state affairs worsened day by day until we reached the present crisis.

sentences.zh: 陛下稍垂日月之明，毋使小人翕聚，以貽善類之禍。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty slightly extend the brightness of sun and moon, and not let petty men gather together to bring calamity upon the good.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty shed a little of the sun's clarity and not let petty men flock together to bring disaster upon the upright.

sentences.zh: 沈炎實、趙與𥲅之腹心爪牙，而任臺臣，甘為之搏擊。

translations.literal: Shen Yanshi and Zhao Yuyu were their trusted claws and fangs, yet were entrusted as censorial officials and willingly struck blows for them.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yanshi and Zhao Yuyu were their henchmen, yet served as censors and willingly did their dirty work.

sentences.zh: 奸黨盤據，血脈貫穿，以欺陛下。

translations.literal: The treacherous faction entrenched itself, their bloodlines interlinked, to deceive Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The faction entrenched itself in a web of kinship to deceive Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 致危亂者，皆此等小人為之。」

translations.literal: Those who brought peril and disorder were all done by such petty men."
translations.idiomatic: It is such petty men who have brought the realm to crisis."

sentences.zh: 又乞令大全致仕，炎等與祠，高鑄羈管州軍。

translations.literal: He also begged that Daquan be ordered to retire, Yan and the rest be given temple appointments, and Gao Zhu be placed under restricted supervision in a prefectural garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that Daquan be forced to retire, that Yan and his circle be given temple sinecures, and that Gao Zhu be placed under restricted supervision.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not act on his request.

sentences.zh: 屬將立度宗為太子，潛密奏云：「臣無彌遠之材，忠王無陛下之福。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Duzong was about to be established as crown prince, Qian secretly memorialized: "Your servant lacks Miyuan's talent; Prince Zhong lacks Your Majesty's blessing."
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong was about to be named crown prince, Qian secretly wrote: "I lack Shi Miyuan's ability, and Prince Zhong lacks Your Majesty's blessing."

sentences.zh: 帝怒潛，卒以炎論劾落職。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry with Qian; in the end, on Yan's impeachment, he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged; on Shen Yan's impeachment Qian was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 命下，中書舍人洪芹繳還詞頭，不報，謫建昌軍，尋徙潮州，責授化州團練使、循州安置。

translations.literal: When the order was issued, Secretariat Drafter Hong Qin returned the draft edict and it went unanswered; Qian was banished to Jianchang Army, soon transferred to Chaozhou, and demoted to Militia Commissioner of Huazhou with residence assigned at Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, drafter Hong Qin returned the draft without effect; Qian was exiled to Jianchang, then moved to Chaozhou, and finally demoted to militia commissioner of Huazhou and confined at Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 潛預知死日，語人曰：「吾將逝矣，夜必雷風大作。」

translations.literal: Qian foreknew the day of his death and told others: "I am about to depart; tonight there will surely be great thunder and wind."
translations.idiomatic: Qian foretold the day of his death, telling others: "I am about to die; tonight there will be thunder and a great storm."

sentences.zh: 已而果然，四鼓開霽，撰遺表，作詩頌，端坐而逝。

translations.literal: And so it was; at the fourth watch the sky cleared; he composed his final memorial, wrote verses of praise, and passed away sitting upright.
translations.idiomatic: It happened as he said; at the fourth watch the sky cleared. He wrote his final memorial and a hymn of praise, then died sitting upright.

sentences.zh: 時景定三年五月也。

translations.literal: It was the fifth month of the third year of Jingding.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the fifth month of the third year of Jingding.

sentences.zh: 循人聞之，咨嗟悲慟。

translations.literal: When the people of Xun heard it, they sighed and grieved in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xun, hearing of his death, mourned him with deep grief.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年，追復元官，仍還執政恩數。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou his original offices were posthumously restored, and the privileges of a chief minister were still returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Deyou his former offices were posthumously restored along with the privileges of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 明年，以太府卿柳岳請贈諡，特贈少師。

translations.literal: The next year, on the request of Director of the Palace Storehouse Liu Yue to grant a posthumous title, he was specially posthumously made Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, at the request of palace storehouse director Liu Yue, he was posthumously granted the title Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 程元鳳

translations.literal: Cheng Yuanfeng
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanfeng

sentences.zh: 程元鳳，字申甫，徽州人。

translations.literal: Cheng Yuanfeng, courtesy name Shenfu, was a native of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanfeng, whose courtesy name was Shenfu, came from Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 紹定元年進士，調江陵府教授。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the first year of Shaoding, he was assigned as Professor at Jiangling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Shaoding and was appointed professor at Jiangling prefecture.

sentences.zh: 端平元年，差江西轉運司干辦公事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Duanping he was assigned as Administrative Clerk in the Jiangxi Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duanping he was assigned as clerk in the Jiangxi transport commission.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 淳祐元年，遷禮、兵二部架閣，以父老不忍去側，遷太學正，以祖諱辭，改國子錄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunyou he was transferred to Archivist in the Ministries of Rites and War; because his aged father could not bear to be parted from him, he was moved to Director of the Imperial Academy, declined on account of his grandfather's taboo name, and was changed to Recorder of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunyou he became archivist in the ministries of rites and war, but when his elderly father could not bear to be separated from him he was made director of the imperial academy; he declined because of his grandfather's taboo name and was reassigned as recorder of the directorate of education.

sentences.zh: 父憂，服闋，遷太學博士，改宗學博士。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he observed mourning; when mourning ended he was transferred to Erudite of the Imperial Academy and changed to Erudite of the Imperial Clan School.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death and the end of mourning he became erudite of the imperial academy, then erudite of the imperial clan school.

sentences.zh: 以《詩》、《禮》講榮王府。

translations.literal: He lectured at the Rong Prince's establishment on the Book of Songs and the Book of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the Book of Songs and the Book of Rites at the household of Prince Rong.

sentences.zh: 旁諷曲諭，隨事規正，多所裨益，王亦傾心敬聽。

translations.literal: With indirect admonition and gentle instruction he corrected matters as they arose and brought much benefit; the prince also gave his heart and listened respectfully.
translations.idiomatic: Through gentle hints and tactful counsel he corrected the prince on many points, and the prince listened to him with full respect.

sentences.zh: 輪對，極論世運剝復之機及人主所當法天者。

translations.literal: In rotation audience he spoke at length on the turning points of decline and revival in the world's fortune and on what the ruler should take from Heaven as his model.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he spoke at length on the cycles of decline and renewal in history and on how the ruler should model himself on Heaven.

sentences.zh: 理宗覽之曰：「有古遺直風。」

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong read it and said: "There is the air of the upright remonstrators of old."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong read his memorial and said, "This has the spirit of the blunt remonstrators of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 六年，進秘書丞兼權刑部郎官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was advanced to Assistant Director of the Secretariat, concurrently acting Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to assistant director of the secretariat with concurrent acting duties in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 七年，兼權右司郎官，遷著作郎，仍權右司郎官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was concurrently acting Director of the Right Section, promoted to Compiler, and still held acting appointment as Director of the Right Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he served concurrently as acting director of the right section, was promoted to compiler, and retained his acting post in the right section.

sentences.zh: 輪對，指陳時病尤激切，當國者以為厲己。

translations.literal: In rotation audience he pointed out the ills of the age with especial vehemence; those in power took it as aimed at themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he denounced the ills of the age with unusual force, and those in power took it as a personal attack.

sentences.zh: 丐外，知饒州。

translations.literal: He begged for an outside post and was made Prefect of Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a post outside the capital and was appointed prefect of Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 郡初罹水災，元鳳訪民疾苦，夙夜究心，修城堞，置義阡，寬誅求，察誣證。

translations.literal: The prefecture had just suffered flood disaster; Yuanfeng inquired into the people's hardships and devoted himself day and night, repaired walls and battlements, established public burial grounds, eased exactions, and examined false accusations.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had just been struck by flood; Yuanfeng investigated the people's suffering, worked day and night, repaired the walls, established public cemeteries, eased levies, and reviewed false charges.

sentences.zh: 進江、淮、荊、浙、福建、廣南都大提點坑冶，仍兼知饒州冶司，歲有冬夏帳銀，悉舉以補郡積年諸稅斂之不足者。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Commissioner for Mining in Jiang, Huai, Jing, Zhe, Fujian, and Guangnan, still concurrently managing the Raozhou mining office; each year there were winter and summer account silvers, all of which he applied to make up the prefecture's long-standing shortfalls in various taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand mining commissioner for the Jiang, Huai, Jing, Zhe, Fujian, and Guangnan circuits, while still overseeing Raozhou's mining office; he devoted all seasonal mining revenues to cover the prefecture's chronic tax shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 芝生治所，眾以治行之致，元鳳曰：「五穀熟則民蒙惠，此不足異也。」

translations.literal: A fungus plant grew at his government office; the multitude attributed it to his good governance, but Yuanfeng said: "When the five grains ripen the people receive benefit—this is nothing extraordinary."
translations.idiomatic: A lingzhi fungus appeared at his yamen; people took it as a sign of good rule, but Yuanfeng said, "When the harvest is good the people benefit—that is nothing unusual."

sentences.zh: 召奏事，辭，不允，遷右曹郎官。

translations.literal: He was summoned to report on affairs, declined, was not permitted, and was transferred to Director of the Right Section.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to report at court, he declined but was overruled and transferred to director of the right section.

sentences.zh: 疏言實學、實政、國本、人才、吏治、生民、財計、兵威八事。

translations.literal: He memorialized on eight matters: solid learning, solid government, the foundation of the state, talent, official administration, the living people, fiscal planning, and military strength.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on eight topics: practical learning, practical governance, the foundations of the state, talent, official conduct, the welfare of the people, finance, and military power.

sentences.zh: 尋兼右司郎官，拜監察御史兼崇政殿說書。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Director of the Right Section and appointed Investigating Censor, concurrently Lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served concurrently as director of the right section and was appointed investigating censor with concurrent lectureship at the Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 丞相鄭清之久專國柄，老不任事，台官潘凱、吳燧合章論列，清之不悅，改遷之，二人不拜命去。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor Zheng Qingzhi had long monopolized state power and, in old age, could not handle affairs; censors Pan Kai and Wu Sui jointly memorialized against him; Qingzhi was displeased and had them transferred, and the two men refused the appointments and left.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Zheng Qingzhi had long held power alone and, grown old, neglected his duties; censors Pan Kai and Wu Sui jointly impeached him; Qingzhi, displeased, had them transferred, and both refused their new posts and resigned.

sentences.zh: 元鳳上疏斥清之罪，其言明白正大，凱、燧得召還。

translations.literal: Yuanfeng submitted a memorial denouncing Qingzhi's crimes; his words were clear and upright, and Kai and Sui were recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng memorialized denouncing Qingzhi's offenses in plain and forceful terms, and Kai and Sui were recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 有事於明堂，元鳳疏言「祈天以實不以文」。

translations.literal: When there were rites at the Bright Hall, Yuanfeng memorialized that "one should pray to Heaven with substance, not with ornament."
translations.idiomatic: When rites were held at the Bright Hall, Yuanfeng wrote that Heaven should be addressed with sincerity, not empty ceremony.

sentences.zh: 又言邊備，謂「當申儆軍實，以起積玩之勢。」

translations.literal: He also spoke on frontier defense, saying that "the military must be sternly alerted and its substance strengthened, to rouse the long-accumulated habit of complacency."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged frontier defense, saying the army must be sharply warned and its strength restored to break years of complacency.

sentences.zh: 及言濫刑之敝。

translations.literal: He also spoke on the harm of excessive punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke on the abuse of harsh punishments.

sentences.zh: 十二年，拜右正言兼侍講，以祖諱辭。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Right Remonstrator with concurrent Lecturer, but declined on account of his grandfather's taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed right remonstrator with concurrent lectureship but declined because of his grandfather's taboo name.

sentences.zh: 詔權以右補闕繫銜。

translations.literal: An edict authorized him to use the title of Right Supplementation Censor as his formal rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered that he hold the acting title of right supplementation censor.

sentences.zh: 上疏論格心之學，謂「革士大夫之風俗，當革士大夫之心術。」

translations.literal: He memorialized on the learning of rectifying the mind, saying that "to reform the customs of scholar-officials, one must reform the inner dispositions of scholar-officials."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the discipline of rectifying the mind, arguing that to reform official custom one must first reform officials' inner motives.

sentences.zh: 至於文敝、邊儲、人才、民心、儲將帥、救災異，莫不盡言。

translations.literal: On literary decadence, frontier stores, talent, popular hearts, storing up generals, and relieving strange calamities, there was nothing he did not speak of fully.
translations.idiomatic: On literary decline, frontier supplies, talent, popular morale, building up generals, and responding to disasters, he left nothing unsaid.

sentences.zh: 余晦以從父天錫恃恩妄作，三學諸生伏闕上書白其罪狀，司業蔡抗又力言之，元鳳數其罪劾之。

translations.literal: Yu Hui, relying on his father's younger brother Tianxi's favor, acted recklessly; students of the three academies knelt at the palace gate to memorialize his crimes; Vice Director Cai Kang also spoke forcefully; Yuanfeng enumerated his crimes and impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Hui abused the favor of his uncle Tianxi; students of the three academies knelt at the palace gate to accuse him, and vice director Cai Kang spoke out as well; Yuanfeng listed his crimes and impeached him.

sentences.zh: 奏上，以晦為大理少卿，抗為宗正少卿。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Hui was made Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review and Kang Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was acted on, Hui was made vice director of the court of judicial review and Kang vice director of the imperial clan court.

sentences.zh: 元鳳又上疏留抗而黜晦，以安士心。

translations.literal: Yuanfeng again memorialized to retain Kang and dismiss Hui, so as to settle the minds of scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng memorialized again to keep Kang in place and remove Hui, so as to calm the students.

sentences.zh: 乃命抗仍兼司業，晦予郡。

translations.literal: Kang was then ordered to remain concurrently Vice Director, and Hui was given a prefectural post.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was ordered to remain vice director, and Hui was sent to a prefecture.

sentences.zh: 升殿中侍御史，仍兼侍講。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Attending Censor, still concurrently Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attending censor while retaining his lectureship.

sentences.zh: 京城災，疏言：「輟土木無益之役，以濟暴露之民；

translations.literal: When disaster struck the capital, he memorialized: "Suspend useless building works of earth and wood to relieve the people left exposed;
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck the capital he wrote: "Halt useless construction projects to aid the homeless;

sentences.zh: 移緇流泛濫之恩，以給顛沛之眾。

translations.literal: shift the indiscriminate favors granted to the clergy to supply the people in desperate flight.
translations.idiomatic: redirect indiscriminate favors to the clergy toward those driven from their homes.

sentences.zh: 務行寬大之政，固結億兆之心。

translations.literal: Strive to practice a generous policy and firmly bind the hearts of the millions.
translations.idiomatic: Practice a generous policy to win the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 旁招俊乂，而私昵無濫及之恩；

translations.literal: Recruit the worthy on every side, while private favorites receive no indiscriminate favor;
translations.idiomatic: Recruit the worthy broadly, while favorites receive no undue favor;

sentences.zh: 屏去奸私，而貪黷無覆出之患。

translations.literal: remove the treacherous and selfish, so that the greedy and corrupt have no chance to reappear.
translations.idiomatic: drive out the corrupt so that greed cannot return.

sentences.zh: 謹便嬖之防，而不使之弄權；

translations.literal: Guard carefully against favorites, and do not let them play with power;
translations.idiomatic: Guard against favorites and keep them from wielding power;

sentences.zh: 抑恩澤之請，而不至於無節。」

translations.literal: restrain requests for favors and grants, so that they do not become unbounded."
translations.idiomatic: restrain petitions for favors so that grants do not run without limit."

sentences.zh: 言多剴切。

translations.literal: His words were mostly incisive and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: His words were sharp and forthright throughout.

sentences.zh: 蜀境與沅、靖交急，朝廷欲擇重臣出鎮上流，用徐敏子易蜀帥及用向士璧為鎮撫。

translations.literal: The Shu frontier and Yuan and Jing were in urgent crisis; the court wished to choose a weighty minister to go out and guard the upper Yangzi, using Xu Minzi to replace the Shu commander and Xiang Shibi as pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: With Shu and the Yuan and Jing regions in crisis, the court sought a senior minister to command the upper Yangzi, replacing the Shu commander with Xu Minzi and appointing Xiang Shibi as pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元鳳請下荊南，調兵援蜀，移呂文德上沅、靖。

translations.literal: Yuanfeng requested that troops be sent down from Jingnan to reinforce Shu and that Lü Wende be moved up to Yuan and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng asked that troops from Jingnan be sent to aid Shu and that Lü Wende be moved to Yuan and Jing.

sentences.zh: 進依前職，簽書樞密院事兼權參知政事，進參知政事，尋進拜右丞相兼樞密使，進封新安郡公。

translations.literal: He was advanced in his former rank, made Junior Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs with concurrent acting Vice Grand Councilor, then promoted to Vice Grand Councilor, soon appointed Right Grand Councilor with concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Xin'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in his former rank to junior signatory at the Bureau of Military Affairs and acting vice grand councilor, then vice grand councilor, soon right grand councilor with command of military affairs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 力辭，御筆勉諭，猶周回累日而後治事。

translations.literal: He strove to decline; the emperor's own brush urged and instructed him, yet he still hesitated for many days before taking up affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He strongly declined, but the emperor's own hand urged him on; he still hesitated for days before accepting office.

sentences.zh: 疏奏正心、待臣、進賢、愛民、備邊、守法、謹微、審令八事。

translations.literal: He memorialized on eight matters: rectifying the mind, treating ministers, advancing the worthy, loving the people, preparing the frontier, observing the law, being careful in small things, and examining edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on eight themes: rectifying the mind, treating ministers properly, promoting talent, caring for the people, securing the frontier, upholding the law, attending to small matters, and scrutinizing edicts.

sentences.zh: 高、孝、光、寧四朝國史未就，奏轉任尤焴領其事，纂修成之。

translations.literal: The national histories of the four reigns of Gao, Xiao, Guang, and Ning were not yet complete; he memorialized to transfer You Yun to take charge of the task, and the compilation was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The national histories of the Gaozong, Xiaozong, Guangzong, and Ningzong reigns were unfinished; he had You Yun placed in charge, and the compilation was completed.

sentences.zh: 會丁大全謀奪相位，元鳳力辭，授觀文殿大學士判福州、福建安撫使。

translations.literal: When Ding Daquan plotted to seize the chief ministership, Yuanfeng strove to decline and was appointed Grand Academician of the Guanwen Hall with charge of Fuzhou and Pacification Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Daquan plotted to seize power, Yuanfeng resigned and was made grand academician of the Guanwen Hall with jurisdiction over Fuzhou and pacification commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 又力辭，依前職，提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He again strove to decline, kept his former rank, and was made Superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He declined again, retained his former rank, and was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 開慶兵興，上手疏收人心、重賞罰、團結民兵數事。

translations.literal: When war arose in Kaiqing, he submitted a memorial to the emperor on winning popular hearts, emphasizing rewards and punishments, and organizing local militia, among other matters.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in the Kaiqing era he memorialized the emperor on winning hearts, enforcing rewards and punishments, and organizing local militia.

sentences.zh: 俄起判平江府兼淮、浙發運使。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised to take charge of Pingjiang Prefecture, concurrently Transport Commissioner for Huai and Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to govern Pingjiang with concurrent duties as transport commissioner for Huai and Zhe.

sentences.zh: 四上章乞免。

translations.literal: He memorialized four times begging to be excused.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized four times asking to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 三年，御筆趣行，奏免修明局米五萬石。

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor's brush urged him to proceed; he memorialized to remit fifty thousand piculs of grain for the Xiuming Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the emperor ordered him to take office; he secured a remission of fifty thousand piculs of grain for the Xiuming Bureau.

sentences.zh: 拜特進，依前職。

translations.literal: He was appointed Special Advancement, in his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted special advancement while retaining his former duties.

sentences.zh: 充醴泉觀兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was made Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey with concurrent Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commissioner of the Liquan Abbey with concurrent lectureship.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，進少保。

translations.literal: When Emperor Duzong took the throne, he was advanced to Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong ascended the throne, he was promoted to junior guardian.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜少傅、右丞相兼樞密使，進封吉國公，以言罷，依舊少保、觀文殿大學士、醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Junior Tutor, Right Grand Councilor with concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Ji; because of criticism he was dismissed and kept his former posts of Junior Guardian, Grand Academician of the Guanwen Hall, and Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became junior tutor, right grand councilor, and military commissioner, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji; impeached, he was dismissed but retained his posts as junior guardian, grand academician of the Guanwen Hall, and commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 乞致仕，不許。

translations.literal: He begged to retire; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 四年，罷觀使，以守少保、觀文殿大學士致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was relieved of his abbey commission and retired as Junior Guardian and Grand Academician of the Guanwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was relieved of his abbey post and retired as junior guardian and grand academician of the Guanwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 卒，遺表聞，帝震悼輟朝，特贈少師。

translations.literal: He died; when his final memorial was reported, the emperor was shaken with grief and suspended court, specially posthumously making him Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died; when his final memorial reached the throne the emperor mourned and suspended court, posthumously granting him the title Junior Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 元鳳之在政府也，一契家子求貳令，元鳳謝之曰：「除授須由資。」

translations.literal: While Yuanfeng was in the government, a son of a family connected by marriage sought a secondary magistracy; Yuanfeng declined, saying: "Appointment must follow qualifications."
translations.idiomatic: While Yuanfeng was in office, a relative by marriage sought a secondary magistracy; Yuanfeng refused, saying, "Appointments must follow proper qualifications."

sentences.zh: 其人累請不許，乃以先世為言。

translations.literal: The man repeatedly begged and was not granted, then spoke of former generations.
translations.idiomatic: The man pressed him repeatedly, then appealed to their families' past ties.

sentences.zh: 元鳳曰：「先公疇昔相薦者，以某粗知恬退故也。

translations.literal: Yuanfeng said: "Your late father recommended me in former days because I had some rough knowledge of quiet withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng said, "Your late father recommended me long ago because he saw that I valued modest withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 今子所求躐次，豈先大夫意哉？

translations.literal: What you now seek skips ranks—would that be your late father's intent?
translations.idiomatic: What you ask now skips proper rank—would your father have wanted that?

sentences.zh: 矧以國家官爵報私恩，某所不敢。」

translations.literal: How much less may I use the state's offices and titles to repay private favor—that is what I dare not do."
translations.idiomatic: Still less would I use state office to repay a private debt—that I dare not do."

sentences.zh: 有嘗遭元鳳論列者，其後見其可用，更薦拔之，每曰：「前日之彈劾，成其才也；

translations.literal: There was one whom Yuanfeng had once impeached; later, seeing him usable, he recommended and promoted him again, always saying: "The impeachment of former days made his talent;
translations.idiomatic: A man he had once impeached, seeing him later prove capable, he recommended and promoted again, saying, "My earlier impeachment helped form his talent;

sentences.zh: 今日之擢用，盡其才也。」

translations.literal: today's promotion exhausts his talent."
translations.idiomatic: today's appointment puts his talent fully to use."

sentences.zh: 所著《訥齋文集》若干卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Collected Works of the Reticent Studio in several juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left behind the Collected Works of the Reticent Studio in several fascicles.

sentences.zh: 江萬里

translations.literal: Jiang Wanli
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wanli

sentences.zh: 江萬里，字子遠，都昌人。

translations.literal: Jiang Wanli, courtesy name Ziyuan, was a native of Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wanli, whose courtesy name was Ziyuan, came from Duchang.

sentences.zh: 自其父燁始業儒。

translations.literal: From his father Ye onward the family took up Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian study began in his family with his father Ye.

sentences.zh: 大父璘，鄉稱善人，其鄰史知縣者誇其能杖嘩健士，璘俯首不答，歸語燁曰：「史祖父故寒士，今居官以杖士人自憙，於我心有不釋然。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lin was called a good man in the village; a neighbor who was magistrate named Shi boasted of his ability to beat rowdy strongmen with the staff; Lin bowed his head and did not answer, then returned home and told Ye: "Magistrate Shi's grandfather was once a poor scholar; now in office he takes pleasure in beating gentlemen with the staff—my heart cannot be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lin was known locally as a good man. A neighbor who was county magistrate named Shi boasted of beating rowdy men with his staff; Lin bowed in silence, then told Ye at home, "Magistrate Shi's family were once poor scholars; now he delights in beating gentlemen with the staff—I cannot approve.

sentences.zh: 審爾，史氏且不昌，汝其戒之。」

translations.literal: If it is so, the Shi clan will not prosper—take warning."
translations.idiomatic: If that is so, the Shi line will not prosper—take heed."

sentences.zh: 是夕燁妻陳夢一貴人入其家，曰：「以汝家長有善言，故來。」

translations.literal: That night Ye's wife Chen dreamed that a noble person entered their house, saying: "Because the elder of your house spoke good words, I have come."
translations.idiomatic: That night Ye's wife Chen dreamed that a noble visitor entered their home and said, "Because the head of your household spoke rightly, I have come."

sentences.zh: 已而有娠，生萬里。

translations.literal: Soon after she was with child and bore Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after she conceived and gave birth to Wanli.

sentences.zh: 少神雋，有鋒穎，連舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In youth he was spiritually keen, with a sharp edge, and passed the provincial examinations in succession.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was brilliant and sharp-witted and passed the provincial examinations in succession.

sentences.zh: 入太學，有文聲。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial Academy and had a reputation in letters.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the imperial academy and gained a literary reputation.

sentences.zh: 理宗在潛邸，嘗書其姓名幾研間。

translations.literal: When Emperor Lizong was in his hidden residence, he once wrote Wanli's name on his desk.
translations.idiomatic: When Lizong was still heir apparent, he once wrote Wanli's name on his desk.

sentences.zh: 以舍選出身，歷池州教授沿江制置司準備差遣，兩浙安撫司干辦公事。

translations.literal: Entering office through selection from the hostel, he served as Professor at Chizhou, Prepared Agent of the Yangzi Defense Commission, and Administrative Clerk in the Two-Zhe Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Entering service through hostel selection, he served as professor at Chizhou, prepared agent on the Yangzi defense commission, and clerk in the Two-Zhe pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 召試館職，累遷著作佐郎、權尚左郎官兼樞密院檢詳文字。

translations.literal: He was summoned to examination for an academy post and was repeatedly promoted to Assistant Compiler, acting Director of the Left Section with concurrent Examiner of Documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to qualify for an academy post, he rose to assistant compiler and acting director of the left section with concurrent duties examining documents at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 知吉州，創白鷺洲書院，兼提舉江西常平茶鹽。

translations.literal: As Prefect of Jizhou he founded the Bailuzhou Academy and was concurrently Commissioner for Ever-Normal Granaries, Tea, and Salt in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Jizhou he founded the Bailuzhou Academy and concurrently oversaw ever-normal granaries, tea, and salt in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 召為屯田郎官，未行，遷直秘閣、江西轉運判官兼權知隆興府。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Public Works for Fields, but before he went was transferred to Direct Attendant of the Secretariat, Transport Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi, and concurrently acting Prefect of Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as director in the fields section of the Ministry of Public Works, he was transferred before taking up the post to direct attendant of the secretariat, Jiangxi transport vice commissioner, and acting prefect of Longxing.

sentences.zh: 創宗濂書院。

translations.literal: He founded the Zonglian Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Zonglian Academy.

sentences.zh: 遷考功郎官，命旋寢。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel for Merit, but the order was soon withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director in the merit section of the Ministry of Personnel, but the appointment was soon rescinded.

sentences.zh: 久之，以駕部郎官召，遷尚右兼侍講。

translations.literal: After a long while he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of War for Chariots, then transferred to Director of the Right Section with concurrent Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was summoned as director in the chariots section and promoted to director of the right section with concurrent lectureship.

sentences.zh: 史嵩之罷相，拜監察御史，仍兼侍講。

translations.literal: When Shi Songzhi was dismissed as chief councilor, Wanli was appointed Investigating Censor, still concurrently Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Songzhi left the chief ministership, Wanli was appointed investigating censor while retaining his lectureship.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷右正言、殿中侍御史，又遷侍御史，未及拜。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Right Remonstrator and Palace Attending Censor, then again to Attending Censor, but had not yet assumed the post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to right remonstrator and palace attending censor, then to attending censor, but had not yet taken up the latter appointment.

sentences.zh: 萬里器望清峻，論議風采傾動一時，帝眷注尤厚。

translations.literal: Wanli's bearing and reputation were pure and lofty; his discourse and presence swayed the age, and the emperor's favor toward him was especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli's bearing was lofty and his reputation pure; his speeches stirred the court, and the emperor favored him above most.

sentences.zh: 嘗丐祠、省母疾，不許。

translations.literal: He once begged for a temple sinecure to visit his mother's illness; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He once asked for a temple post to nurse his ill mother, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 屬弟萬頃奉母歸南康，旋以母病聞，萬里不俟報馳歸，至祁門得訃。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wanqing was escorting their mother back to Nankang when word came of her illness; Wanli did not wait for permission but rushed home, and at Qimen received news of her death.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Wanqing was escorting their mother to Nankang when news came that she was ill; Wanli rushed home without waiting for leave and learned of her death at Qimen.

sentences.zh: 而議者謂萬里母死，秘不奔喪，反挾妾媵自隨，於是側目萬里者，相與騰謗。

translations.literal: But critics said that when Wanli's mother died he secretly failed to rush to mourning and instead took concubines with him; those who had looked askance at Wanli then joined in spreading slander.
translations.idiomatic: Critics claimed that when his mother died he concealed the news and failed to observe mourning, traveling instead with concubines; his enemies seized on this to spread slander.

sentences.zh: 萬里無以自解，坐是閒廢者十有二年。

translations.literal: Wanli had no way to clear himself and on this account remained idle and dismissed for twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to clear himself, he remained out of office for twelve years.

sentences.zh: 後陸德輿嘗辨其非辜於帝前。

translations.literal: Later Lu Deyu once argued before the emperor that he was not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lu Deyu pleaded his innocence before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 賈似道宣撫兩浙，辟參謀官。

translations.literal: When Jia Sidao was Pacification Commissioner of the Two Zhe, he recruited Wanli as Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Sidao pacified the Two Zhe, he recruited Wanli as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 及似道同知樞密院，為京湖宣撫大使，以萬里帶行寶章閣待制，為參謀官。

translations.literal: When Sidao became Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Grand Pacification Commissioner of Jing and Hu, he made Wanli Attendant Gentleman of the Traveling Baozhang Pavilion as Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Sidao became vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and grand pacification commissioner of Jing and Hu, he appointed Wanli traveling attendant of the Baozhang Pavilion as his staff officer.

sentences.zh: 大元兵圍鄂，似道以右丞兼樞密使移軍漢陽，萬里遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Great Yuan troops besieged E; Sidao, as Right Vice Councilor with concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs, moved the army to Hanyang; Wanli was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan forces besieged Ezhou, Sidao as right vice councilor and military commissioner moved his army to Hanyang, and Wanli was made vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 似道入相，萬里兼國子祭酒、侍讀。

translations.literal: When Sidao entered the chief ministership, Wanli was concurrently Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When Sidao became chief councilor, Wanli served concurrently as chancellor of the directorate of education and lecturer.

sentences.zh: 入對，遷權吏部尚書，又拜端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: On entering audience he was transferred to acting Minister of Personnel, then appointed Academician of the Duanming Hall, Co-Signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and concurrently Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In audience he was made acting minister of personnel, then academician of the Duanming Hall, co-signatory at the Bureau of Military Affairs, and tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 隨以言者去官。

translations.literal: Soon, because of critics, he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed after criticism from the censors.

sentences.zh: 後以原職知建寧府兼權福建轉運使。

translations.literal: Later, in his former rank, he was made Prefect of Jianning with concurrent acting Transport Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed prefect of Jianning with concurrent acting transport commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 已而，加資政殿學士，依舊職，知福州兼福建安撫使。

translations.literal: Before long he was given Academician of the Zizheng Hall, kept his former duties, and was made Prefect of Fuzhou with concurrent Pacification Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made academician of the Zizheng Hall and appointed prefect of Fuzhou with concurrent pacification commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 度宗即位，召同知樞密院事，又兼權參知政事，遷參知政事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Duzong took the throne, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then concurrently acting Vice Grand Councilor, and promoted to Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When Duzong ascended the throne, Wanli was recalled as vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then acting vice grand councilor, and finally vice grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 萬里始雖俯仰容默，為似道用，然性峭直，臨事不能無言。

translations.literal: At first Wanli, though bowing and holding his tongue in accommodation, was used by Sidao; yet his nature was steep and upright, and facing affairs he could not keep silent.
translations.idiomatic: At first Wanli accommodated himself to Sidao, bowing and holding his tongue, yet his nature was upright and sharp, and he could not keep silent when matters arose.

sentences.zh: 似道常惡其輕發，故每人不能久在位。

translations.literal: Sidao always hated his rash speech, so each time he could not long remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao always resented his bluntness, so Wanli never long kept any post.

sentences.zh: 似道以去要君，帝初即位，呼為師相，至涕泣拜留之。

translations.literal: Sidao used threatening to leave to hold the emperor hostage; when the emperor first ascended the throne, he called him teacher-minister, even weeping and bowing to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao threatened resignation to coerce the throne; when Duzong first ascended, he called Sidao his teacher-minister and wept and bowed to keep him from leaving.

sentences.zh: 萬里以身掖帝云：「自古無此君臣禮，陛下不可拜，似道不可復言去。」

translations.literal: Wanli supported the emperor with his body and said: "Since antiquity there has been no such rite between ruler and minister; Your Majesty must not bow, and Sidao must speak no more of leaving."
translations.idiomatic: Wanli steadied the emperor and said, "No ruler and minister in history ever observed such a rite; Your Majesty must not bow, and Sidao must not speak of leaving again.

sentences.zh: 似道不知所為，下殿舉笏謝萬里曰：「微公，似道幾為千古罪人。」

translations.literal: Sidao did not know what to do, descended the hall, raised his tablet, and thanked Wanli, saying: "But for you, sir, Sidao would almost have become a criminal through the ages."
translations.idiomatic: Sidao, at a loss, left the hall, raised his tablet, and thanked Wanli: "But for you, I would have been condemned for all time.

sentences.zh: 然以此益忌之。

translations.literal: Yet because of this he hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Sidao hated him all the more for it.

sentences.zh: 帝在講筵，每問經史疑義及古人姓名，似道不能對，萬里常從旁代對。

translations.literal: At the lecture hall, whenever the emperor asked about doubtful points in the classics and history or the names of ancients, Sidao could not answer; Wanli often answered from the side.
translations.idiomatic: During lectures, whenever the emperor asked about obscure points in the classics or the names of ancients, Sidao could not answer and Wanli often supplied the reply from the side.

sentences.zh: 時王夫人頗知書，帝語夫人以為笑。

translations.literal: At the time Lady Wang was quite learned in books; the emperor told the lady about it as a joke.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang was well read at the time, and the emperor told her the story as a jest.

sentences.zh: 似道聞之，積慚怒，謀逐之。

translations.literal: When Sidao heard of it, shame and anger accumulated, and he plotted to drive Wanli out.
translations.idiomatic: When Sidao heard of it, shame and anger piled up, and he plotted to drive Wanli from court.

sentences.zh: 萬里四丐祠，不候報出關。

translations.literal: Wanli four times begged for a temple sinecure and left the pass without waiting for a reply.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli four times asked for a temple post and left the capital without waiting for approval.

sentences.zh: 加資政殿大學士、知慶元府兼沿海制置使，不拜，予祠。

translations.literal: He was given Academician of the Zizheng Hall, Prefect of Qingyuan with concurrent Coastal Defense Commissioner; he did not accept and was granted a temple appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Qingyuan with concurrent coastal defense commissioner, but refused the post and was granted a temple sinecure instead.

sentences.zh: 後二年，知太平州兼提領江淮茶鹽兼江東轉運使，召拜參知政事，進封南康郡公，既至，拜左丞相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: Two years later he was made Prefect of Taiping with concurrent oversight of Jiang-Huai tea and salt and Jiangdong transport commissioner; summoned and appointed Vice Grand Councilor; advanced to Duke of Nankang; on arrival he was appointed Left Chief Councilor with concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was appointed prefect of Taiping with concurrent oversight of Jiang-Huai tea and salt and Jiangdong transport commissioner, then recalled as vice grand councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Nankang; on arrival he was made left chief councilor and military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丐祠，加觀文殿大學士知福州，辭，依舊職，提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He begged for a temple sinecure; he was given Academician of the Guanwen Hall and Prefect of Fuzhou; he declined and kept his former post as Superintendent of the Tongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a temple post and was offered academician of the Guanwen Hall and prefect of Fuzhou, but declined and remained superintendent of the Tongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 又授知潭州、湖南安撫大使，加特進，尋予祠。

translations.literal: He was also appointed Prefect of Tanzhou and Grand Pacification Commissioner of Hunan; given special advanced rank; soon granted a temple appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed prefect of Tanzhou and grand pacification commissioner of Hunan, given special advanced rank, and soon granted a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 時咸淳九年，萬里年七十有六矣。

translations.literal: At the time it was the ninth year of Xianchun; Wanli was seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: It was the ninth year of Xianchun, and Wanli was seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 明年，大元兵渡江，萬里隱草野間，為游騎所執，大詬，欲自戕，既而脫歸。

translations.literal: The next year Great Yuan troops crossed the Yangzi; Wanli hid among fields and wilds; he was seized by roaming cavalry; he cursed loudly and tried to kill himself; then he escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yuan forces crossed the Yangzi; Wanli hid in the countryside, was seized by roaming cavalry, cursed them fiercely and tried to kill himself, then escaped and made his way home.

sentences.zh: 先是，萬里聞襄樊失守，鑿池芝山後圃，扁其亭曰「止水」，人莫諭其意，及聞警，執門人陳偉器手，曰：「大勢不可支，余雖不在位，當與國為存亡。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wanli heard that Xiangyang and Fancheng had fallen, he dug a pool in the rear garden of Zhishan and inscribed the pavilion "Stopping Water"; no one understood his meaning. When he heard the alarm, he took the hand of his disciple Chen Weiqi and said: "The great trend cannot be sustained; though I am not in office, I should live and die with the state."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Xiangyang and Fancheng fell, Wanli dug a pool in the garden behind Zhishan and named the pavilion "Stopping Water," though no one understood why.
