When the alarm came, he took his disciple Chen Weiqi by the hand and said, "The realm cannot be saved; though I hold no office, I must live and die with the state.

sentences.zh: 及饒州城破，軍士執萬頃，索金銀不得，支解之。

translations.literal: When Raozhou city fell, soldiers seized Wanqing, demanded gold and silver but got none, and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: When Raozhou fell, soldiers seized his brother Wanqing, demanded gold and silver, found none, and dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 萬里竟赴止水死。

translations.literal: Wanli finally went to Stopping Water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli finally drowned himself in the Stopping Water pool.

sentences.zh: 左右及子鎬相繼投沼中，積屍如疊。

translations.literal: Attendants and his son Hao successively threw themselves into the pool; corpses piled like stacks.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants and his son Hao followed him into the pool one after another until the bodies lay piled upon one another.

sentences.zh: 翼日，萬里屍獨浮出水上，從者草斂之。

translations.literal: The next day Wanli's corpse alone floated to the surface; followers gave it a rough burial.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wanli's body alone floated to the surface, and his followers buried it with whatever they could find.

sentences.zh: 萬里無子，以蜀人王橚子為後，即鎬也。

translations.literal: Wanli had no son; he took the son of Wang Su of Shu as heir—that was Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli had no son of his own and adopted Wang Su's son from Shu as his heir—this was Hao.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太傅、益國公，後加贈太師，諡文忠。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously given Grand Tutor and Duke of Yiguo; later additionally Grand Preceptor; posthumous title Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When news reached the court, he was posthumously made grand tutor and Duke of Yiguo, later raised to grand preceptor, with the posthumous title Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 萬頃歷守大郡，為提舉江西常平茶鹽，官至正郎。

translations.literal: Wanqing had served as prefect of major commanderies, was Commissioner for Ever-Normal Granaries, Tea, and Salt in Jiangxi, and reached the rank of Regular Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Wanqing had governed major prefectures, served as Jiangxi commissioner for ever-normal granaries, tea, and salt, and reached the rank of regular gentleman.

sentences.zh: 城破時，郴州守趙崇榞寓居城中，亦死之。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Zhao Chongyuan, Prefect of Chenzhou, was lodging in the city and also died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Zhao Chongyuan, prefect of Chenzhou, who was staying in the city, died as well.

sentences.zh: 寶祐元年，兼國史編修、實錄檢討兼權兵部侍郎，試司農卿兼中書門下省檢正諸房公事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoyou he was concurrently Compiler of the National History, Examiner of the Veritable Records with concurrent acting Vice Minister of War, tested as Minister of Revenue for Agriculture with concurrent Examiner of Various Bureaus in the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoyou, Yue served concurrently as compiler of the national history and examiner of the veritable records with acting vice minister of war, was tested as minister of revenue for agriculture, and concurrently examined documents in the various bureaus of the secretariat-chancellery.

sentences.zh: 疏奏：「願詔大臣相與憂亂而思治，懼危而圖安，哀恫警省，修德行政，摧抑群陰之氣焰，保護微陽之根本。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "I wish Your Majesty would summon the chief ministers to share anxiety over disorder and think on good governance, fear peril and plan security, grieve and be alarmed into self-examination, cultivate virtue and conduct government, suppress the arrogance of all yin forces, and protect the root of the faint yang.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote, "I pray Your Majesty will summon the chief ministers to share anxiety over disorder and seek good governance, fear peril and plan for safety, grieve and be alarmed into self-examination, cultivate virtue and govern well, suppress the arrogance of corrupt forces, and protect the root of what is upright.

sentences.zh: 批札畢杜於私蹊，官賞宏辟於正路。

translations.literal: Let private shortcuts be wholly blocked in written orders, and official rewards and appointments open broadly on the correct path.
translations.idiomatic: Let private favors be wholly shut off in written orders, and official rewards and appointments open broadly on the proper path.

sentences.zh: 使內治明如天日，外治勁如風霆。

translations.literal: Make internal governance bright as the sun, and external governance vigorous as wind and thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Make internal governance clear as daylight and external governance forceful as wind and thunder.

sentences.zh: 則精神運動，陽匯昭蘇，世道昌明，物情熙洽。

translations.literal: Then the spirit will move, yang will gather and revive, the age will prosper, and all feelings will harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Then the spirit will stir, yang will gather and revive, the age will flourish, and all hearts will be at ease.

sentences.zh: 上以迓續天命於譴告之余，下以固結人心於解紐之際。

translations.literal: Above, to meet and continue Heaven's mandate amid reproach and warning; below, to solidify the people's hearts at the moment ties are loosening.
translations.idiomatic: Above, to receive and continue Heaven's mandate amid reproach and warning; below, to bind the people's hearts at the moment the realm is coming undone.

sentences.zh: 其孰能御之。」

translations.literal: Who then could withstand it?"
translations.idiomatic: Who then could stand against it?

sentences.zh: 以右文殿修撰提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: He was made Right Writing Hall Compiler and Superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed compiler of the Right Writing Hall and superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 五年，京湖宣撫大使趙葵辟為判官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Zhao Kui, Grand Pacification Commissioner of Jing and Hu, recruited him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Zhao Kui, grand pacification commissioner of Jing and Hu, recruited him as administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 開慶元年，召赴行在，授集英殿修撰、樞密都承旨、權吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiqing he was summoned to the mobile court and appointed Compiler of the Jiying Hall, Director-in-chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and acting Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiqing he was summoned to the mobile court and made compiler of the Jiying Hall, director-in-chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and acting vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 景定元年，兼同修國史、實錄院同修撰兼侍讀，為真侍郎兼太子左庶子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingding he was concurrently Associate Compiler of the National History, Associate Compiler at the Veritable Records Academy, and Lecturer; he was made full Vice Minister of Personnel with concurrent Left Sub-mentor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingding he concurrently served as associate compiler of the national history, associate compiler at the Veritable Records Academy, and lecturer, was made full vice minister of personnel, and concurrently left sub-mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 極言正論，太子聽而說之，帝聞之甚喜。

translations.literal: He spoke forthright and correct doctrine; the crown prince listened and was pleased; the emperor heard and was greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke with force and principle; the crown prince listened with pleasure, and the emperor was greatly pleased to hear of it.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷禮部尚書，權吏部尚書，加龍圖閣學士、知平江府、淮浙發運使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Minister of Rites and acting Minister of Personnel; he was given Dragon Diagram Hall Academician, Prefect of Pingjiang, and Huai-Zhe Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to minister of rites and acting minister of personnel, and was given dragon diagram hall academician, prefect of Pingjiang, and Huai-Zhe transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，召赴行在，進端明殿學士，提舉佑神觀兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned to the mobile court and advanced to Duanming Hall Academician, Superintendent of the Youshen View with concurrent Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was summoned to the mobile court and promoted to academician of the Duanming Hall and superintendent of the Youshen View with concurrent lecturer.

sentences.zh: 召赴行在。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「今天下所以大壞至此者，正以一私蟠塞，賞罰無章故也。

translations.literal: In a memorial he stated: "The reason the realm has fallen so far is precisely that private interest blocks everything and rewards and punishments are without rule.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote, "The realm has fallen so far precisely because private interest blocks everything and rewards and punishments have no rule.

sentences.zh: 救之之策，在反其所以壞之之由。

translations.literal: The remedy lies in reversing the cause of the ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The remedy is to reverse the very cause of the ruin.

sentences.zh: 大明賞罰，動合乎天，庶幾人心興起，天下事尚可為也。」

translations.literal: Clarify rewards and punishments so that actions accord with Heaven; then perhaps hearts will rise and affairs under Heaven may still be done."
translations.idiomatic: Make rewards and punishments clear so that action accords with Heaven, and perhaps hearts will stir and the realm may yet be saved.

sentences.zh: 因言賈似道誤國喪師之罪，於是始降詔切責似道不忠不孝。

translations.literal: He also spoke of Jia Sidao's crime of misleading the state and losing the army; thereupon an edict first sternly rebuked Sidao for disloyalty and unfilial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He also denounced Jia Sidao's crime of misleading the state and losing the army, whereupon the court for the first time issued an edict sharply rebuking Sidao for disloyalty and unfilial conduct.

sentences.zh: 六月庚子朔，日食，爚奏：「日食不盡僅一分，白晝晦冥者數刻。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, day gengzi, there was a solar eclipse; Yue memorialized: "The eclipse was incomplete by only one fen; daylight was dark for several quarters.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month, day gengzi, there was a solar eclipse; Yue memorialized, "The eclipse fell short of totality by only one fen, yet daylight was dim for several quarters.

sentences.zh: 陰盛陽微，災異未有大於此者。

translations.literal: Yin excessive and yang weak—no portent greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Yin is strong and yang is weak—no omen greater than this.

sentences.zh: 臣待罪首相，上佐天子理陰陽，下遂萬物，外鎮諸侯，皆其職也。

translations.literal: I, your minister, guilty in the chief ministership, above assist the Son of Heaven in harmonizing yin and yang, below extend to all things, and externally pacify the feudal lords—all these are my duties.
translations.idiomatic: I, your minister, stand guilty as chief councilor: above I should assist the Son of Heaven in harmonizing yin and yang, below extend benefit to all things, and externally pacify the feudal lords—all this is my charge.

sentences.zh: 氛祲充塞而未能消，生民塗炭而未能拯，反覆思之，咎實在臣，乞罷黜以答天譴。」

translations.literal: Ominous vapors fill and I cannot dispel them; the people are charred in hardship and I cannot rescue them; turning it over in my mind, the blame truly lies with me; I beg dismissal to answer Heaven's reproach."
translations.idiomatic: Ominous vapors fill the realm and I cannot dispel them; the people suffer charred hardship and I cannot save them; turning it over again and again, the fault is truly mine; I beg to be dismissed to answer Heaven's reproach.

sentences.zh: 答詔不許，第降授金紫光祿大夫而已。

translations.literal: The response edict did not permit it, only demoting him to Grandee of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, demoting him only to grandee of the gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 辭降官，乞罷斥，又不許。

translations.literal: He declined the demotion and begged dismissal; again it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the demotion and again begged to be removed; again the court refused.

sentences.zh: 尋進平章軍國重事，辭，不許。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Grand Coordinator of Military and State Affairs; he declined, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Grand Coordinator of Military and State Affairs. He declined the appointment, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 或請：「出宜中或夢炎出督吳門，否則臣雖老無能為，若效死封疆，亦不敢辭。」

translations.literal: A memorial proposed: "Send Chen Yizhong or Liu Mengyan out to supervise Wu Gate; otherwise, though this subject is old and incapable, if it is to die in service on the frontier, I dare not decline."
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he proposed that either Chen Yizhong or Liu Mengyan be dispatched to take command at Wu Gate; failing that, though he was old and felt himself unequal to the task, he was willing to die defending the frontier if required.

sentences.zh: 詔三省集議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Three Departments to convene for joint deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the Three Departments to meet and deliberate on the matter.

sentences.zh: 乞罷平章事，不許。

translations.literal: He requested dismissal from the post of Grand Coordinator; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be relieved of his post as Grand Coordinator, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 京學生上書詆宜中，宜中亦上疏乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Students of the Imperial University submitted a memorial attacking Chen Yizhong; Chen Yizhong also submitted a memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Students of the Imperial University submitted a memorial denouncing Chen Yizhong, and Chen Yizhong in turn memorialized the throne, asking to be allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 初，宜中在相位，政事多不關白爚，或謂京學之論，實爚嗾之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yizhong held the position of chief minister, many affairs of government were not reported to Yue for consultation. Some said the criticism from the Imperial University was in fact instigated by Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yizhong had been chief minister, he had often handled state business without consulting Wang Yue. Some claimed that the university students' attack on him had really been instigated by Wang.

sentences.zh: 七月壬辰，詔：「給、舍之奏三入，爚與宜中必難共處，兼爚近奏乞免平章侍經筵，辭氣不平，誠有如人言者矣。」

translations.literal: On the day renchen of the seventh month, an edict stated: "The memorials of the drafting and reviewing officers have thrice been submitted. Yue and Yizhong surely cannot coexist. Moreover, Yue's recent memorial requesting relief from the grand coordinatorship and attendance at the lecture hall was couched in an aggrieved tone—it is indeed as people have said."
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day of the seventh month, an edict declared: "The memorials from the drafting and reviewing officers have now been submitted three times. Wang Yue and Chen Yizhong clearly cannot serve together. Wang Yue's recent request to be relieved of his grand coordinatorship and his duties at the imperial lecture hall was plainly resentful in tone; what people have been saying appears to be true."

sentences.zh: 遂罷爚平章，依前少保、特授觀文殿大學士充醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yue was removed from the grand coordinatorship, retaining his former title of Junior Guardian, and was specially appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, serving as commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue was accordingly stripped of his grand coordinatorship. He kept his former rank as Junior Guardian and was given the honorific appointment of Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 爚為人清修剛勁，似道歸天台葬母，過新昌，爚獨不見之。

translations.literal: Yue as a man was pure in conduct, upright and firm. When Sidao returned to Tiantai to bury his mother and passed through Xinchang, Yue alone refused to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue was a man of austere integrity and uncompromising strength. When Jia Sidao went back to Tiantai to bury his mother and passed through Xinchang, Wang Yue alone refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 後以元老入相位，值國勢危亡之際，天下所屬望也，而卒與宜中不協而去云。

translations.literal: Later, as a senior statesman he entered the position of chief minister at a time when the nation's situation was critical and perilous—the object of the empire's hopes—yet in the end, failing to harmonize with Yizhong, he departed, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned to high office as a senior statesman at the very moment the dynasty stood on the brink of ruin, bearing the hopes of the empire—but in the end he could not work with Chen Yizhong and left office, or so it is recorded.

sentences.zh: 章鑒，字公秉，分寧人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian, courtesy name Gongbing, was a native of Fenning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, styled Gongbing, was from Fenning.

sentences.zh: 以別院省試及第，累官中書舍人、侍左郎官、崇政殿說書，進簽書樞密院事兼權參知政事，遷同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Having passed the provincial special examination at a separate branch, he rose through the offices of Secretariat Drafter, attendant of the Left Bureau, and lecturer at the Hall for Promoting Governance, then advanced to Deputy Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs with concurrent acting Vice Grand Counselor, and was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination through a separate branch and rose through posts as Secretariat Drafter, attendant in the Left Bureau, and lecturer at the Hall for Promoting Governance. He was then promoted to Deputy Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs with concurrent acting appointment as Vice Grand Counselor, and later became Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 咸淳十年，王爚拜左丞相，鑒拜右丞相，併兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianchun, Wang Yue was appointed Left Grand Counselor and Jian Right Grand Counselor; both concurrently held the post of Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Xianchun era, Wang Yue was named Left Grand Counselor and Zhang Jian Right Grand Counselor; each also served concurrently as Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，大元兵逼臨安，鑒託故徑去。

translations.literal: The following year, when the Great Yuan army pressed upon Lin'an, Jian used a pretext and left directly.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, as the Yuan forces closed in on Lin'an, Zhang Jian made an excuse and slipped away without ceremony.

sentences.zh: 遣使亟召還朝，既至，罷相予祠。

translations.literal: Envoys were urgently dispatched to summon him back to court; once he arrived, he was removed from the chief ministership and granted a nominal temple post.
translations.idiomatic: The court urgently sent envoys to recall him. When he returned, he was dismissed from the chief ministership and given a nominal temple appointment instead.

sentences.zh: 殿帥韓震之死，鑒與曾淵子明震無他。

translations.literal: At the death of Han Zhen, commander of the palace guard, Jian and Zeng Yuanzi testified that Zhen had no other ulterior intent.
translations.idiomatic: After the palace guard commander Han Zhen was killed, Zhang Jian and Zeng Yuanzi had attested that Han bore no treasonous motive.

sentences.zh: 至是，御史王應麟繳其錄黃，謂震有逆謀，鑒與淵子曲芘之。

translations.literal: At this time, Censor Wang Yinglin impeached their recorded draft, declaring that Zhen had had a treasonous plot, and that Jian and Yuanzi had bent the rules to shield him.
translations.idiomatic: Now Censor Wang Yinglin attacked the draft they had approved, charging that Han Zhen had harbored a plot of rebellion and that Zhang Jian and Zeng Yuanzi had twisted the record to protect him.

sentences.zh: 坐是削一官，放歸田裡。

translations.literal: For this he was demoted one rank and sent back to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: For this offense he was stripped of one rank and released to live in retirement in the countryside.

sentences.zh: 後有告鑒家匿寶璽者，霜晨，鑒方擁敗衾臥，兵士至，大索其室，惟敝篋貯一玉杯，余無一物，人頗嘆其清約。

translations.literal: Later someone reported that Jian's household was hiding a precious seal. On a frosty morning, Jian was just lying wrapped in a tattered quilt when soldiers arrived and searched his rooms thoroughly; only a worn case holding a jade cup was found—nothing else—and people greatly admired his frugality and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone accused Zhang Jian's household of concealing an imperial seal. One frosty morning, as he lay beneath a threadbare quilt, soldiers arrived and turned his house upside down. All they found was a shabby box containing a single jade cup and nothing else; many marvelled at his plain, abstemious life.

sentences.zh: 鑒在朝日，號寬厚，然與人多許可，士大夫目為「滿朝歡」云。

translations.literal: In Jian's days at court he was known as magnanimous, yet he assented to everyone readily, and the scholar-officials called him "Universal Approval," it is said.
translations.idiomatic: While at court Zhang Jian had a reputation for largeness of spirit, but he was quick to agree with everyone, and officials nicknamed him "Universal Approval"—not entirely as a compliment, it is said.

sentences.zh: 陳宜中

translations.literal: Chen Yizhong
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong

sentences.zh: 陳宜中，字與權，永嘉人也。

translations.literal: Chen Yizhong, courtesy name Yuquan, was a man of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong, styled Yuquan, was a native of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 少甚貧，而性特俊拔。

translations.literal: In youth he was very poor, yet by nature exceptionally sharp and elevated.
translations.idiomatic: He grew up in great poverty, but his nature was unusually keen and forceful.

sentences.zh: 有賈人推其生時，以為當大貴，以女妻之。

translations.literal: A merchant, extrapolating from his birth time, deemed that he was destined for great eminence and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: A merchant who cast his birth chart decided he was fated for high rank and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 既入太學，有文譽。

translations.literal: Once he entered the Imperial University, he gained a literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: After entering the Imperial University, he won a reputation for literary talent.

sentences.zh: 寶祐中，丁大全以戚里婢婿事權幸盧允升、董宋臣，困得寵於理宗，擢為殿中侍御史，在台橫甚。

translations.literal: In the Baoyou era, Ding Daquan, having become son-in-law through a maid of the imperial clan, served the favorites Lu Yunshang and Dong Songchen, and thereby won the favor of Emperor Lizong; he was promoted to Palace Censor and was exceedingly overbearing at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoyou era, Ding Daquan—who had married into the imperial clan through a maid-servant—attached himself to the favorites Lu Yunshang and Dong Songchen and eventually won Emperor Lizong's trust. Raised to Palace Censor, he ruled the Censorate with brutal arrogance.

sentences.zh: 宜中與黃鏞、劉黻、林測祖、陳宗、曾唯六人上書攻之。

translations.literal: Yizhong, together with Huang Yong, Liu Fu, Lin Cezu, Chen Zong, and Zeng Wei—the six of them—submitted a memorial attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong joined Huang Yong, Liu Fu, Lin Cezu, Chen Zong, and Zeng Wei in a memorial denouncing him—the group later known as the Six.

sentences.zh: 大全怒，使監察御史吳衍劾宜中，削其籍，拘管他州。

translations.literal: Daquan in anger had Investigating Censor Wu Yan impeach Yizhong, struck him from the register, and placed him under detention in another prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Daquan retaliated by having Investigating Censor Wu Yan impeach Chen Yizhong, removing him from the university rolls and confining him under guard in another prefecture.

sentences.zh: 司業率十二齋生，冠帶送之橋門之外，大全益怒，立碑學中，戒諸生亡妄議國政，且令自後有上書者，前廊生看詳以牒報檢院。

translations.literal: The Vice Director of Studies led the students of the twelve halls, in cap and belt, to escort him beyond the Bridge Gate. Daquan grew still angrier; he erected a stele in the university, warning the students not to presumptuously discuss state affairs, and ordered that thereafter any who submitted memorials should have them reviewed by the front-hall students and reported by memorandum to the Inspection Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Director of Studies led students from all twelve halls, dressed in full regalia, to escort Chen Yizhong as far as the Bridge Gate. Daquan, furious, had a stele erected in the university forbidding students to meddle in state affairs and decreed that from then on any student memorials must first be reviewed by front-hall students and forwarded by memo to the Inspection Office.

sentences.zh: 由是，士論翕然稱之，號為「六君子」。

translations.literal: From this, public opinion among the scholar-officials united in praising them, and they were called the "Six Gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-official opinion rallied to their side, and the six were hailed as the "Six Gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 宜中謫建昌軍。

translations.literal: Yizhong was demoted to Jianchang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong was banished to Jianchang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大全既竄，丞相吳潛奏還之。

translations.literal: Once Daquan had been banished, Grand Counselor Wu Qian memorialized for his recall.
translations.idiomatic: After Ding Daquan was driven out, Grand Counselor Wu Qian petitioned for Chen Yizhong's restoration.

sentences.zh: 賈似道入相，復為之請，有詔六人皆免省試令赴。

translations.literal: When Jia Sidao entered the chief ministership, he again petitioned on their behalf; an edict ordered that all six be exempted from the provincial examination and summoned to attend.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Sidao became chief minister, he too petitioned on their behalf, and an edict exempted all six from the provincial examination and summoned them to proceed.

sentences.zh: 景定三年，廷試，而宜中中第二人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingding, at the palace examination, Yizhong placed second.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination in the third year of Jingding, Chen Yizhong finished second.

sentences.zh: 六人之中，宜中尤達時務。

translations.literal: Among the six, Yizhong was especially adept at current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Of the six, Chen Yizhong was particularly skilled in the affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 由紹興府推官、戶部架閣、秘書省正字、校書郎，數年遷監察御史。

translations.literal: From judicial officer of Shaoxing Prefecture, Archivist of the Ministry of Revenue, Corrector of the Secretariat, and Proofreader, within several years he was transferred to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as judicial officer in Shaoxing Prefecture, archivist in the Ministry of Revenue, corrector in the Secretariat, and proofreader, and within a few years was promoted to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 程元鳳再相，似道恐其侵權，欲去之。

translations.literal: When Cheng Yuanfeng again became chief minister, Sidao feared he would encroach on his power and wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Yuanfeng returned as chief minister, Jia Sidao feared a challenge to his authority and sought to force him out.

sentences.zh: 宜中首劾元鳳縱丁大全肆惡，基宗社之禍。

translations.literal: Yizhong was the first to impeach Yuanfeng for indulging Ding Daquan in wicked conduct, laying the foundation for disaster to the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong led the charge, impeaching Cheng Yuanfeng for allowing Ding Daquan free rein in evil—the root, he argued, of the dynasty's ruin.

sentences.zh: 命格，除太府卿。

translations.literal: The appointment was blocked; he was instead made Director of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: The dismissal was blocked, and Cheng Yuanfeng was reassigned as Director of the Imperial Storehouse instead.

sentences.zh: 宜中亦自請外，為江東提舉茶鹽常平公事。

translations.literal: Yizhong also requested an outside appointment of his own accord, becoming Commissioner for Tea, Salt, and Ever-Normal Granaries in Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong also volunteered for a provincial post, becoming Commissioner for Tea, Salt, and Ever-Normal Granaries in Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 四年，改浙西提刑。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to Judicial Commissioner of Western Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the era he was transferred to Judicial Commissioner for Western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 五年，召為崇政殿說書，累遷禮部侍郎兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was summoned as lecturer at the Hall for Promoting Governance, and by successive promotions became Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent appointment as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled to serve as lecturer at the Hall for Promoting Governance and rose step by step to Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent appointment as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 七年，閩闕帥，以敷文閣待制、知福州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, with Fujian lacking a commander, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Hall Spreading Culture and prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when Fujian lacked a military governor, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Hall Spreading Culture and made prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 在官得民心，歲余入為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In office he won the people's hearts; after slightly more than a year he entered the capital as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect he won the people's trust, and a little over a year later he was recalled to the capital as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜簽書樞密院事兼權參知政事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he was appointed Deputy Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs with concurrent acting Vice Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed Deputy Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs with concurrent acting status as Vice Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 德祐元年，陞同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Deyou, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Deyou he was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二月，似道喪師蕪湖，乃以宜中知樞密院兼參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second month, after Sidao lost his army at Wuhu, Yizhong was made Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs with concurrent appointment as Vice Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, after Jia Sidao's army was destroyed at Wuhu, Chen Yizhong was appointed Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 已而翁應龍自軍中歸，宜中問似道所在，應龍以不知對。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Weng Yinglong returned from the army; Yizhong asked where Sidao was, and Yinglong answered that he did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, Weng Yinglong came back from the front. Chen Yizhong asked where Jia Sidao was, and Weng Yinglong replied that he did not know.

sentences.zh: 宜中以為似道已死，即上疏乞正似道誤國之罪。

translations.literal: Yizhong supposed that Sidao was already dead and immediately submitted a memorial requesting that Sidao's crime of misguiding the state be formally adjudicated.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Jia Sidao was dead, Chen Yizhong at once memorialized the throne, demanding that Sidao be formally charged with having ruined the country.

sentences.zh: 似道行時，以所親信韓震總禁兵，人有言震欲以兵劫遷者，宜中召震計事，伏壯士袖鐵椎擊殺之，以示不黨於似道。

translations.literal: While Sidao was on the road, he had entrusted his close confidant Han Zhen with overall command of the forbidden troops. Someone said Zhen intended to use the army to force the court's relocation. Yizhong summoned Zhen to discuss affairs, hid strong men with iron maces in their sleeves, and had them strike and kill him, to show that he was not aligned with Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: As Jia Sidao fled, he had left his trusted follower Han Zhen in command of the palace guard. Rumors spread that Han planned to use the troops to coerce the court into flight. Chen Yizhong summoned Han to a conference, concealed strongmen armed with iron maces in their sleeves, and had Han beaten to death—making a show of breaking with Sidao.

sentences.zh: 時右丞相章鑒宵遁，曾淵子等請命宜中攝丞相事。

translations.literal: At that time Right Grand Councillor Zhang Jian fled by night; Zeng Yuanzi and others requested orders for Yizhong to act as Grand Councillor in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Right Grand Councillor Zhang Jian fled under cover of night, and Zeng Yuanzi and others asked that Chen Yizhong be authorized to serve as acting Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 詔以王爚為左丞相，拜宜中特進、右丞相。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Wang Yue as Left Grand Councillor and invested Yizhong as Special Advancement and Right Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Wang Yue Left Grand Councillor and invested Chen Yizhong as Special Advancement and Right Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 四月，爚還朝論事，即與宜中不合。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Yue returned to court to discuss affairs and immediately fell out with Yizhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Wang Yue returned to court to discuss affairs and at once clashed with Chen Yizhong.

sentences.zh: 台臣孫嶸叟請竄籍潛說友、吳益、李珏，宜中以為「簿錄非盛世事，祖宗忠厚，未嘗輕用之。

translations.literal: Censorate official Sun Yaosou requested banishment and registration of Qian Shuoyou, Wu Yi, and Li Jue. Yizhong said: "Seizure and registration of property is not something done in flourishing ages; our ancestors were generous and never used it lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Sun Yaosou petitioned to banish and register the property of Qian Shuoyou, Wu Yi, and Li Jue. Chen Yizhong argued: "Confiscation and registry of assets is no practice of a flourishing age; our ancestors were magnanimous and never applied it lightly.

sentences.zh: 珏方召入朝，遽加重刑，恐後無以示信」。

translations.literal: Jue has just been summoned to court; to impose severe punishment so hastily would make it hard afterward to show good faith."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jue has only just been recalled to court; to heap severe punishment on him so abruptly would leave us no credible way to win trust afterward."

sentences.zh: 爚力爭，以為當如嶸叟議。

translations.literal: Yue argued forcefully that they should follow Yaosou's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue pressed the point vigorously, insisting they should adopt Sun Yaosou's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 會留夢炎自湖南入朝爚與宜中俱乞罷政，請以夢炎為相。

translations.literal: Just then Liu Mengyan came to court from Hunan; both Yue and Yizhong requested to resign from government and asked that Mengyan be made Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Liu Mengyan arrived at court from Hunan; both Wang Yue and Chen Yizhong asked to resign and proposed that Liu Mengyan be made Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后乃以宜中為左丞相，夢炎為右丞相，爚進平章軍國重事。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager then made Yizhong Left Grand Councillor, Mengyan Right Grand Councillor, and advanced Yue to Concurrently Oversee State and Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager then appointed Chen Yizhong Left Grand Councillor, Liu Mengyan Right Grand Councillor, and promoted Wang Yue to Concurrent Overseer of State and Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 爚拜命，即日僦民居，以丞相府讓宜中，宜中上疏，以為「一辭一受，何以解天下之譏」，亦去。

translations.literal: Upon receiving the appointment, Yue that same day rented a private residence and yielded the Grand Councillor's mansion to Yizhong. Yizhong submitted a memorial saying: "One man resigns and another accepts—how can this dispel the ridicule of all under Heaven?" He too resigned.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yue accepted the appointment, he rented a private house that very day and turned the Grand Councillor's residence over to Chen Yizhong. Chen Yizhong memorialized: "One man steps down and another takes his place—how can that answer the scorn of the empire?" He resigned as well.

sentences.zh: 遣使數輩遮留之，始至。

translations.literal: Several envoys were dispatched to intercept and detain him; only then did he arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Several messengers were sent to stop and hold him back; only then did he come.

sentences.zh: 時命張世傑等四道進師，二丞相都督軍馬而不出督。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Shijie and others were ordered to advance in four columns, yet the two Grand Councillors supervised the armies without going out to command them in person.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Shijie and others were ordered to advance on four fronts, while the two Grand Councillors held overall command of the armies without going out to lead them in person.

sentences.zh: 爚請以一丞相建閫吳門，以護諸將；

translations.literal: Yue requested that one Grand Councillor establish headquarters at Wumen to protect the generals;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue asked that one Grand Councillor establish a command headquarters at Wumen to shield the generals;

sentences.zh: 不然，則已請行。

translations.literal: otherwise, he himself requested to take the field.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise he himself asked to take the field.

sentences.zh: 宜中愧，始與夢炎上疏乞行邊。

translations.literal: Ashamed, Yizhong at last joined Mengyan in memorializing to beg to go to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Chen Yizhong finally joined Liu Mengyan in memorializing to beg permission to go to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 事下公卿議不決。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the high officials for discussion, but no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was sent down to the chief ministers for deliberation, but no decision was reached.

sentences.zh: 七月，世傑等兵果敗於焦山。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Shijie's forces were indeed defeated at Jiaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zhang Shijie's army was indeed defeated at Jiaoshan.

sentences.zh: 爚奏言：「事無重於兵，今二相並建都督，廟算指授，臣不得而知。

translations.literal: Yue memorialized: "Nothing is graver than military affairs. Now two Grand Councillors jointly establish a command headquarters; the plans ordained in the temple and the orders given—your subject cannot know them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue memorialized: "Nothing is more urgent than military affairs. Two Grand Councillors now jointly establish a command headquarters, yet the plans made in council and the orders issued—your subject cannot know them.

sentences.zh: 比者，六月出師，諸將無統。

translations.literal: Recently, when the army marched out in the sixth month, the generals had no unified command.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched out in the sixth month, the generals had no single commander over them.

sentences.zh: 臣豈不知吳門距京不遠，而必為此請者，蓋大敵在境，非陛下自將則大臣開督。

translations.literal: Your subject is not unaware that Wumen is not far from the capital; yet he must make this request because a great enemy is on the border—in such cases, unless Your Majesty personally leads the troops, a chief minister must open a command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject knows full well that Wumen is not far from the capital; yet I must make this request because a great enemy stands on our borders—in such a crisis, unless Your Majesty leads the armies yourself, a chief minister must take command in the field.

sentences.zh: 今世傑以諸將心力不一而敗，不知國家尚堪幾敗邪？

translations.literal: Now Shijie has been defeated because the generals' hearts and efforts were not united—does the state not know how many more defeats it can bear?
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhang Shijie has been defeated because the generals' hearts and efforts were divided—does the state know how many more defeats it can survive?

sentences.zh: 臣既不得其職，又不得其言，乞罷免。」

translations.literal: Your subject has neither obtained his proper function nor has his words heeded; he requests dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has neither been given his proper role nor had his words heeded; I beg to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: The request was denied.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 爚子□乃嗾京學生伏闕上書，數宜中過失數十事，其略以為：「趙溍、趙與鑒皆棄城遁，宜中乃借使過之說，以報私恩。

translations.literal: Yue's son incited Capital students to kneel at the palace gate and submit a memorial, listing dozens of Yizhong's faults. In summary it said: "Zhao Yin and Zhao Yuqian both abandoned their cities and fled, yet Yizhong used the excuse of special missions to let them off, repaying private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue's son incited Capital students to kneel at the palace gate and submit a memorial enumerating dozens of Chen Yizhong's failings. In essence it charged: "Zhao Yin and Zhao Yuqian both abandoned their cities and fled, yet Chen Yizhong used the pretext of special missions to shield them, repaying private debts of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 令狐概、潛說友皆以城降，乃受其包苴而為之羽翼。

translations.literal: Linghu Kai and Qian Shuoyou both surrendered their cities, yet he accepted their bribes and became their patron.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Kai and Qian Shuoyou both surrendered their cities, yet he took their bribes and became their protector.

sentences.zh: 文天詳率兵勤王，信讒而沮撓之。

translations.literal: Wen Tianxiang led troops to aid the throne, yet Yizhong believed slanders and obstructed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tianxiang raised troops to rescue the throne, yet Chen Yizhong believed slanders against him and blocked his efforts.

sentences.zh: 似道喪師誤國，陽請致罰而陰佑之。

translations.literal: Sidao lost armies and misled the state; Yizhong outwardly asked that he be punished while secretly protecting him.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao had lost armies and ruined the state; Chen Yizhong publicly demanded his punishment while secretly shielding him.

sentences.zh: 大兵薄國門，勤王之師乃留之京城而不遣。

translations.literal: When the great army pressed on the capital gates, the troops raised to aid the throne were kept in the capital and not dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy army pressed on the capital gates, the forces raised to rescue the throne were kept in the city and never sent out.

sentences.zh: 宰相當出督，而畏縮猶豫，第令集議而不行。

translations.literal: Grand Councillors ought to go out and command, yet he cowered and hesitated, merely ordering discussions that were never carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillors ought to go out and take command, yet he shrank back in hesitation, calling only for meetings that were never acted upon.

sentences.zh: 呂師夔狼子野心，而使之通好乞盟。

translations.literal: Lü Shigao has the heart of a wolf cub; yet Yizhong sent him to treat for peace and beg alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Shigao has the heart of a wolf cub, yet Chen Yizhong sent him to negotiate peace and plead for alliance.

sentences.zh: 張世傑步兵而用之於水，劉師勇水兵而用之於步，指授失宜，因以敗事。

translations.literal: Zhang Shijie was an infantry commander yet was used on water; Liu Shiyong was a naval commander yet was used on land—commands were wrongly assigned, and so affairs were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie was an infantry commander yet was deployed on water; Liu Shiyong was a naval commander yet was deployed on land—commands were misassigned, and defeat followed.

sentences.zh: 臣恐誤國將不止於一似道也。」

translations.literal: Your subjects fear that those who mislead the state will not be limited to Sidao alone."
translations.idiomatic: We fear that those who ruin the state will not be limited to Jia Sidao alone."

sentences.zh: 臨安府捕逮京學生。

translations.literal: The Lin'an prefecture arrested the Capital students.
translations.idiomatic: The Lin'an prefectural office arrested the Capital students.

sentences.zh: 召之亦不至。

translations.literal: They were summoned but did not come.
translations.idiomatic: They were summoned but did not appear.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后自為書遺其母楊，使勉諭之，宜中始乞以祠官入侍，乃拜醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager herself wrote a letter to his mother Yang, asking her to exhort him; only then did Yizhong beg to serve at court as a temple official and was appointed Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager herself wrote to his mother, Lady Yang, asking her to counsel him; only then did Chen Yizhong beg to attend court as a temple commissioner and was appointed Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 十月壬寅，始造朝，尋為右丞相，然事已去矣。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day of the tenth month he at last came to court; soon he was made Right Grand Councillor, but the situation was already beyond recovery.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day of the tenth month he at last came to court; soon he was made Right Grand Councillor, but the cause was already lost.

sentences.zh: 宜中倉皇發京城民為兵，民年十五以上者皆籍之，人皆以為笑。

translations.literal: Yizhong hastily conscripted the people of the capital as soldiers, registering all males fifteen and above; everyone regarded it as laughable.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong hastily conscripted the people of the capital, registering every male fifteen and older; all regarded it as absurd.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣張全合尹玉、麻士龍兵援常州，玉與士龍皆戰死，全不發一矢，奔還。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he dispatched Zhang Quan, together with Yin Yu and Ma Shilong, to reinforce Changzhou. Yu and Shilong both died in battle; Quan did not release a single arrow and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent Zhang Quan, together with Yin Yu and Ma Shilong, to reinforce Changzhou. Yu and Shilong both fell in battle; Quan did not loose a single arrow and fled back.

sentences.zh: 文天祥請誅全，宜中釋不問。

translations.literal: Wen Tianxiang requested that Quan be executed; Yizhong released him without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tianxiang demanded that Zhang Quan be executed; Chen Yizhong released him without investigation.

sentences.zh: 已而，常州破，兵薄獨松關，鄰邑望風皆遁。

translations.literal: Before long Changzhou fell; the enemy army pressed on Dusong Pass, and neighboring districts fled at the rumor of its approach.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Changzhou fell; the enemy pressed on Dusong Pass, and neighboring districts fled at the first rumor of their approach.

sentences.zh: 宜中遣使如軍中請和不得，即率群臣入宮請遷都，太皇太后不可。

translations.literal: Yizhong sent envoys to the enemy camp to sue for peace but failed; he then led the ministers into the palace to request relocation of the capital, which the Grand Empress Dowager refused.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong sent envoys to the enemy camp to sue for peace but failed; he then led the ministers into the palace to beg that the capital be moved, which the Grand Empress Dowager refused.

sentences.zh: 宜中痛哭請之，太皇太后乃命裝俟升車，給百官路費銀。

translations.literal: Yizhong wept and begged for it; the Grand Empress Dowager then ordered preparations for her to board the carriage and granted silver for travel expenses to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong wept and pleaded; the Grand Empress Dowager then ordered preparations for her to board the carriage and granted silver travel funds to the officials.

sentences.zh: 及暮，宜中不入，太皇太后怒曰：「吾初不欲遷，而大臣數以為請，顧欺我邪？」

translations.literal: At dusk Yizhong did not enter. The Grand Empress Dowager angrily said: "At first I did not wish to relocate, yet the high ministers repeatedly pleaded for it—were they merely deceiving me?
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Chen Yizhong did not appear. The Grand Empress Dowager angrily said: "At first I did not wish to move the capital, yet the high ministers pleaded again and again—were they merely deceiving me?

sentences.zh: 脫簪珥擲之地，遂閉閣，群臣求內引，皆不納。

translations.literal: She removed her hairpins and earrings and threw them to the ground, then shut her chamber; the ministers sought an audience but were all refused.
translations.idiomatic: She tore off her hairpins and earrings and threw them to the floor, then shut her chamber; the ministers sought an audience but were all turned away.

sentences.zh: 蓋宜中實以明日遷，倉卒奏陳失審耳。

translations.literal: It seems Yizhong had actually planned to relocate the next day; in haste his memorial had been ill considered.
translations.idiomatic: Apparently Chen Yizhong had actually planned to move the court the next day; in his haste the memorial had been poorly judged.

sentences.zh: 宜中初與大元丞相伯顏期會軍中，既而悔之，不果往。

translations.literal: Yizhong had at first arranged to meet in camp with Bayan, Grand Councillor of the Great Yuan; afterward he regretted it and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong had at first agreed to meet Bayan, Grand Councillor of the Great Yuan, in the field; afterward he regretted it and did not go.

sentences.zh: 伯顏將兵至皋亭山，宜中宵遁，陸秀夫奉二王入溫州，遣人召宜中。

translations.literal: Bayan led his troops to Gaoting Mountain; Yizhong fled by night. Lu Xiufu escorted the two princes into Wenzhou and sent men to summon Yizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan led his army to Gaoting Mountain; Chen Yizhong fled by night. Lu Xiufu escorted the two princes into Wenzhou and sent men to summon Chen Yizhong.

sentences.zh: 宜中至溫州，而其母死。

translations.literal: Yizhong arrived at Wenzhou, but his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong reached Wenzhou, but his mother died.

sentences.zh: 張世傑舁其棺舟中，遂與俱入閩中。

translations.literal: Zhang Shijie had the coffin carried onto a boat, and together they entered Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie had the coffin carried onto a boat, and together they entered Fujian.

sentences.zh: 益王立，復以為左丞相。

translations.literal: When Prince Yi was enthroned, Yizhong was again made Left Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yi was enthroned, Chen Yizhong was again made Left Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 井澳之敗，宜中欲奉王走占城，乃先如占城諭意，度事不可為，遂不反。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Jing'ao, Yizhong wished to escort the prince to flee to Champa; he first went to Champa himself to explain his intentions, judged the enterprise impossible, and never returned.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Jing'ao, Chen Yizhong wished to take the prince and flee to Champa; he went to Champa first to explain his plan, judged the venture impossible, and never returned.

sentences.zh: 二王累使召之，終不至。

translations.literal: The two princes repeatedly sent to summon him, but he never came.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes repeatedly summoned him, but he never came.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年，大軍伐占城，宜中走暹，後沒於暹。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan, the Great Army attacked Champa; Yizhong fled to Siam and later died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of the Zhiyuan era, the Yuan army attacked Champa; Chen Yizhong fled to Siam and later died there.

sentences.zh: 宜中為人多術數，少為縣學生，其父為吏受贓當黥，宜中上書溫守魏克愚請貸之。

translations.literal: Yizhong was skilled in many occult arts; in youth he was a county student. His father, a clerk, took bribes and was liable to branding; Yizhong wrote to Wenzhou prefect Wei Keyu begging leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong was versed in many occult arts; in youth he was a county student. His father, a clerk, had taken bribes and was liable to be branded; Chen Yizhong wrote to the Wenzhou prefect Wei Keyu begging leniency.

sentences.zh: 克愚以為黠吏，卒置之法。

translations.literal: Keyu regarded him as a cunning clerk and ultimately had him punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Keyu regarded the father as a cunning clerk and in the end had him punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 其後宜中為浙西提刑，克愚郊迎，宜中報禮不書銜，亦云「部下民陳某」，克愚皇恐不敢受，袖而謝之。

translations.literal: Later, when Yizhong was Intendant of Judicial Affairs in western Zhejiang, Keyu went out to the suburbs to welcome him. Yizhong's return courtesy omitted his official title and merely said "Chen, a subject under you." Keyu was terrified and did not dare accept it; he put it in his sleeve and declined.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Chen Yizhong served as Intendant of Judicial Affairs in western Zhejiang, Wei Keyu went out to the suburbs to welcome him. Chen Yizhong's return letter omitted his official title and read only "Chen, a man under your jurisdiction." Keyu was terrified and dared not accept it; he tucked it in his sleeve and declined.

sentences.zh: 宜中陽禮之，而陰摭其過，無所得。

translations.literal: Yizhong outwardly treated him with courtesy while secretly searching for faults against him, but found none.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong treated him courteously in public while secretly hunting for faults against him, but found none.

sentences.zh: 其後，克愚發賈德生冒借官木事，忤似道，廢罷家居。

translations.literal: Later Keyu exposed Jia Desheng's fraudulent borrowing of government timber, offending Sidao; he was dismissed and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei Keyu exposed Jia Desheng's fraudulent use of government timber, offending Jia Sidao; he was dismissed and lived at home in retirement.

sentences.zh: 宜中入，乃極言克愚居鄉不法事，似道令章鑒劾之，貶嚴州。

translations.literal: When Yizhong entered court, he repeatedly denounced Keyu's unlawful conduct in the countryside; Sidao had Zhang Jian impeach him and he was demoted to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yizhong entered court, he repeatedly denounced Keyu's misconduct in the countryside; Jia Sidao had Zhang Jian impeach him, and he was demoted to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 克愚之死，宜中擠之為多。

translations.literal: In Keyu's death, Yizhong's persecution played a large part.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong's persecution contributed greatly to Wei Keyu's death.

sentences.zh: 論曰：「孔子曰：「才難，不其然乎？」

translations.literal: The critique says: "Confucius said: 'Talent is hard to find—is it not so?'
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: "Confucius said, 'Talent is hard to find—is it not so?'

sentences.zh: 理宗在位長久，命相實多其人，若吳潛之忠亮剛直，財數人焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Lizong reigned for a long time and appointed many capable Grand Councillors; those like Wu Qian in loyalty, integrity, and firm uprightness numbered only a few.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong reigned for a long time and appointed many men as Grand Councillors, yet those of Wu Qian's loyal brightness and firm uprightness were only a few.

sentences.zh: 潛論事雖近於訐，度宗之立，謀議及之，潛以正對，人臣懷顧望為子孫地者能為斯言哉？

translations.literal: Qian's remonstrances, though close to impeachment, when the choice of Emperor Duzong was under discussion he answered with principled forthrightness—what courtier scheming for his descendants' advantage could speak thus?
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qian's remonstrances, though bordering on impeachment, were principled; when the enthronement of Emperor Duzong was under discussion he answered with upright candor—what courtier scheming to secure his descendants' future could have spoken as he did?

sentences.zh: 程元鳳謹飭而有餘而乏風節，尚為賈似道所諅。

translations.literal: Cheng Yuanfeng was diligent and restrained beyond measure yet lacked moral backbone, and still was slighted by Jia Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanfeng was meticulous and self-restrained to a fault yet lacked moral backbone, and even he was belittled by Jia Sidao.

sentences.zh: 江萬里問學德望優於諸臣，不免為似道籠絡，晚年微露鋒，穎輒見擯斥。

translations.literal: Jiang Wanli's learning and moral stature surpassed the other ministers, yet he could not escape being co-opted by Sidao; when in his later years he slightly showed an edge, he was at once driven out.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wanli's learning and moral stature surpassed the other ministers, yet he could not escape Jia Sidao's entanglements; when in his later years he showed even a slight edge, he was at once cast out.

sentences.zh: 士大夫不幸與權奸同朝，自處難矣。

translations.literal: When scholar-officials unfortunately serve in the same court as a powerful villain, conducting themselves properly is difficult indeed.
translations.idiomatic: When scholar-officials are unlucky enough to serve in the same court as a powerful villain, it is hard indeed to conduct themselves with integrity.

sentences.zh: 似道督視江上之師，以國事付王爚、章鑒、陳宜中，蓋取其平時素與己者。

translations.literal: Sidao oversaw the troops on the Yangtze and entrusted state affairs to Wang Yue, Zhang Jian, and Chen Yizhong—choosing those who had always been close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao oversaw the Yangtze armies and entrusted state affairs to Wang Yue, Zhang Jian, and Chen Yizhong—men he had always favored.

sentences.zh: 爚、宜中於其既出，稍欲自異，及聞其敗，乘勢蹙之。

translations.literal: After he departed, Yue and Yizhong slightly wished to distinguish themselves from him; when they heard of his defeat, they seized the moment to press him hard.
translations.idiomatic: After he left, Wang Yue and Chen Yizhong slightly tried to distance themselves from him; when they heard of his defeat, they seized the moment to press him.

sentences.zh: 既而，二人自為矛盾，宋事至此，危急存亡之秋也。

translations.literal: Before long the two turned against each other; the Song cause had reached the autumn of crisis between ruin and survival.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the two turned on each other; the Song had reached the hour when ruin and survival hung in the balance.

sentences.zh: 當國者交歡戮力，猶懼不逮，所為若是，何望其能匡濟乎。

translations.literal: Those holding power ought to join in mutual goodwill and pooled strength, yet even then one fears it may not suffice; when their conduct is like this, how can one hope they will set things right?
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold power ought to join in goodwill and common effort, yet even then one fears it may not be enough; when their conduct is such as this, how can one hope they will save the state?

sentences.zh: 似道誅，爚死，鑒遁，宜中走海島，宋亡。

translations.literal: Sidao was executed, Yue died, Jian fled, Yizhong escaped to sea isles—and the Song perished.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao was executed, Wang Yue died, Zhang Jian fled, Chen Yizhong escaped to the islands—and the Song fell.

sentences.zh: 文天祥

translations.literal: Wen Tianxiang
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tianxiang

sentences.zh: 文天祥，字宋瑞，又字履善，吉之吉水人也。

translations.literal: Wen Tianxiang, courtesy name Songrui and also Lüshan, was a native of Jishui in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tianxiang, courtesy name Songrui and also Lüshan, was a native of Jishui in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 體貌豐偉，美皙如玉，秀眉而長目，顧盼燁然。

translations.literal: His physique was tall and imposing, his complexion fair as jade; he had fine brows and long eyes, and his gaze was radiant.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and imposing, with a fair complexion like jade, fine brows and long eyes, and a gaze that shone with spirit.

sentences.zh: 自為童子時，見學宮所祠鄉先生歐陽修、楊邦乂、胡銓像，皆諡「忠」，即欣然慕之。

translations.literal: From boyhood, when he saw in the school the images of his county's honored elders Ouyang Xiu, Yang Bangyi, and Hu Quan, all posthumously titled "Loyal," he delighted in them and aspired to follow their example.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood, when he saw in the school the portraits of his county's honored elders Ouyang Xiu, Yang Bangyi, and Hu Quan—all posthumously titled "Loyal"—he rejoiced in them and aspired to join their company.

sentences.zh: 曰：「沒不俎豆其間，非夫也。」

translations.literal: He said: "If after death I am not honored among them with sacrificial vessels, I am no true man."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "If after death I am not honored among them with sacrificial vessels, I am no true man."

sentences.zh: 年二十舉進士，對策集英殿。

translations.literal: At age twenty he passed the jinshi examination and answered policy questions in the Hall for Assembling Excellence.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination and answered policy questions in the Hall for Assembling Excellence.

sentences.zh: 時理宗在位久，政理浸怠，天祥以法天不息為對，其言萬餘，不為稿，一揮而成。

translations.literal: The Emperor Lizong had reigned long and governance had gradually slackened; Tianxiang answered on the theme of emulating Heaven's unceasing vigor. His essay ran to more than ten thousand characters; he did not draft it beforehand but wrote it at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Lizong had reigned for many years and governance had gradually slackened; Tianxiang answered on the theme of emulating Heaven's unceasing vigor. His essay ran to more than ten thousand characters; he wrote it at a stroke without drafting it first.

sentences.zh: 帝親拔為第一。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally selected him for first place.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally ranked him first.

sentences.zh: 考官王應麟奏曰：「是卷古誼若龜鑒，忠肝如鐵石，臣敢為得人賀。」

translations.literal: Examiner Wang Yinglin memorialized: "This examination paper's ancient rectitude is like a tortoise mirror; its loyal heart is like iron and stone. Your subject dares congratulate you on gaining such a man."
translations.idiomatic: Examiner Wang Yinglin memorialized: "This examination paper's ancient rectitude is like a tortoise mirror; its loyal heart is like iron and stone. Your subject dares congratulate you on gaining such a man."

sentences.zh: 尋丁父憂，歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he observed mourning for his father's death and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his father's death and returned home.

sentences.zh: 開慶初，大元兵伐宋，宦官董宋臣說上遷都，人莫敢議其非者。

translations.literal: At the start of the Kaiqing era, the Great Yuan army attacked the Song; eunuch Dong Songchen persuaded the Emperor to relocate the capital, and no one dared dispute it.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaiqing era, the Yuan army attacked the Song; the eunuch Dong Songchen persuaded the Emperor to move the capital, and no one dared oppose him.

sentences.zh: 天祥時入為寧海軍節度判官，上書「乞斬宋臣，以一人心」。

translations.literal: Tianxiang had recently entered service as military commissioner adjutant of Ninghai; he memorialized "begging that Songchen be executed to unify the people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang had recently entered service as adjutant to the military commissioner of Ninghai; he memorialized begging that Songchen be executed to unify the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 不報，即自免歸。

translations.literal: There was no response; he at once resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: There was no response; he resigned at once and returned home.

sentences.zh: 後稍遷至刑部郎官。

translations.literal: Later he was gradually promoted to a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was gradually promoted to a secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 宋臣復入為都知，天祥又上書極言其罪，亦不報。

translations.literal: Songchen again entered service as Director of Palace Affairs; Tianxiang again memorialized, speaking at length of his crimes, but again there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: Songchen again entered service as Director of Palace Affairs; Tianxiang again memorialized at length on his crimes, but again received no response.

sentences.zh: 出守瑞州，改江西提刑，遷尚書左司郎官，累為台臣論罷。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Ruizhou, transferred to Jiangxi Intendant of Judicial Affairs, promoted to Secretary in the Left Office of the Ministry of Revenue, and repeatedly dismissed after censorate attacks.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Ruizhou, transferred to Jiangxi Intendant of Judicial Affairs, promoted to Secretary in the Left Office of the Ministry of Revenue, and was repeatedly dismissed after censorate attacks.

sentences.zh: 除軍器監兼權直學士院。

translations.literal: He was appointed Superintendent of the Directorate of Armaments with concurrent acting duty in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Superintendent of the Directorate of Armaments with concurrent acting duty in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 賈似道稱病，乞致仕，以要君，有詔不允。

translations.literal: Jia Sidao claimed illness and begged to retire, coercing the sovereign; an edict refused.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao claimed illness and begged to retire as a way of coercing the sovereign; an edict refused his request.

sentences.zh: 天祥當制，語皆諷似道。

translations.literal: When Tianxiang drafted the edict, every phrase satirized Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianxiang drafted the edict, every phrase satirized Sidao.

sentences.zh: 時內製相承皆呈稿，天祥不呈稿，似道不樂，使臺臣張志立劾罷之。

translations.literal: At the time successive drafters of imperial documents all submitted drafts for approval; Tianxiang did not submit a draft. Sidao was displeased and had censor Zhang Zhili impeach and dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time successive drafters of imperial documents all submitted drafts for approval; Tianxiang did not. Sidao was displeased and had censor Zhang Zhili impeach and dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 天祥既數斥，援錢若水例致仕，時年三十七。

translations.literal: Having been dismissed several times, Tianxiang cited the precedent of Qian Ruoshui to request retirement; he was then thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Having been dismissed several times, Tianxiang cited the precedent of Qian Ruoshui and requested retirement; he was then thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 咸淳九年，起為湖南提刑，因見故相江萬里。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianchun he was recalled as Hunan Intendant of Judicial Affairs and paid a visit to former Grand Councillor Jiang Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xianchun he was recalled as Hunan Intendant of Judicial Affairs and visited the former Grand Councillor Jiang Wanli.

sentences.zh: 萬里素奇天祥志節，語及國事，愀然曰：「吾老矣，觀天時人事當有變，吾閱人多矣，世道之責，其在君乎？

translations.literal: Wanli had long admired Tianxiang's resolve and integrity. When they spoke of state affairs, he said gravely: "I am old. Watching Heaven's signs and human affairs, change must come. I have observed many men; the burden of the age—does it rest upon you?
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wanli had long admired Tianxiang's resolve and integrity. When they spoke of state affairs, he said gravely: "I am old. Watching Heaven's signs and human affairs, change must come. I have seen many men; the burden of the age—does it rest upon you?

sentences.zh: 君其勉之。」

translations.literal: Press on diligently."
translations.idiomatic: Press on with all your strength."

sentences.zh: 十年，改知贛州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to serve as prefect of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was transferred to serve as prefect of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 德祐初，江上報急，詔天下勤王。

translations.literal: At the start of Deyou, urgent reports came from the Yangtze front; an edict summoned all the realm to aid the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Deyou era, urgent reports came from the Yangtze front; an edict summoned the whole realm to aid the throne.

sentences.zh: 天祥捧詔涕泣，使陳繼周發郡中豪傑，並結溪峒蠻，使方興召吉州兵，諸豪傑皆應，有眾萬人。

translations.literal: Tianxiang received the edict with tears, dispatched Chen Jizhou to rally the county's leading men, also allied with tribal chiefs of the mountain passes, and sent Fang Xing to summon troops from Ji Prefecture; all the leading men responded, and he had a force of ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang received the edict with tears, sent Chen Jizhou to rally the county's leading men, also allied with tribal chiefs of the mountain passes, and dispatched Fang Xing to summon troops from Ji Prefecture; all the leading men answered the call, and he raised a force of ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 事聞，以江西提刑安撫使召入衛。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was summoned to guard the capital as Jiangxi Intendant and Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was summoned to guard the capital as Jiangxi Intendant and Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 其友止之，曰：「今大兵三道鼓行，破郊畿，薄內地，君以烏合萬餘赴之，是何異驅群羊而搏猛虎。」

translations.literal: His friend tried to stop him, saying: "Now the great army advances in three columns with beating drums, has broken the capital suburbs, and presses on the interior—you go with a mob of ten thousand-odd. How is this different from driving a flock of sheep to fight a tiger?
translations.idiomatic: A friend tried to stop him, saying: "Now the great army advances in three columns with beating drums, has broken through the capital suburbs, and presses on the interior—you go with a hastily gathered force of ten thousand. How is that different from driving a flock of sheep against a tiger?

sentences.zh: 天祥曰：「吾亦知其然也。

translations.literal: Tianxiang said: "I too know it is so.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang said: "I know that as well.

sentences.zh: 第國家養育臣庶三百餘年，一旦有急，征天下兵，無一人一騎入關者，吾深恨於此，故不自量力，而以身徇之，庶天下忠臣義士將有聞風而起者。

translations.literal: Only that the state has nourished officials and people for more than three hundred years; once an emergency arose and troops were summoned from all the realm, not a single man or horse entered the passes—I deeply resent this. Therefore, not measuring my own strength, I offer my body in sacrifice, hoping that loyal ministers and righteous men throughout the realm will hear of it and rise up.
translations.idiomatic: The state has nourished officials and people for more than three hundred years, yet when crisis came and troops were summoned from across the realm, not a single man or horse answered the call to enter the passes. I deeply resent this. So, without measuring my own strength, I offer myself in sacrifice, in the hope that loyal ministers and righteous men throughout the realm will hear of it and rise up.

sentences.zh: 義勝者謀立，人眾者功濟，如此則社稷猶可保也。」

translations.literal: Where righteousness prevails, plans can be made; where men are many, the work can succeed—thus the altars of state may yet be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Where righteousness prevails, strategy can stand; where the people are many, the task can be done. In this way the altars of state may yet be preserved."

sentences.zh: 天祥性豪華，平生自奉甚厚，聲伎滿前。

translations.literal: Tianxiang was by nature fond of luxury; throughout his life he maintained himself very richly, with singers and performers filling his presence.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang was by nature fond of luxury; throughout his life he lived in considerable style, with singers and performers always at hand.

sentences.zh: 至是，痛自貶損，盡以家貲為軍費。

translations.literal: At this point he harshly reduced himself, devoting all his household wealth to military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: At this point he stripped his life to the bone, putting all his household wealth toward military expenses.

sentences.zh: 每與賓佐語及時事，輒流涕，撫幾言曰：「樂人之樂者憂人之憂，食人之食者死人之事。」

translations.literal: Whenever he spoke with guests and aides about current affairs, he would weep, strike the armrest, and say: "Those who rejoice in others' joy should grieve over others' grief; those who eat others' food should die for others' affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he spoke with guests and aides about current affairs, he would weep, beat the armrest, and say: "Those who share in the people's joy must share in their sorrow; those who live on the state's grain must die in its service.

sentences.zh: 八月，天祥提兵至臨安，除知平江府。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Tianxiang led troops to Lin'an and was appointed prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Tianxiang led troops to Lin'an and was appointed prefect of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 時以丞相宜中未還朝，不遣。

translations.literal: At the time because Grand Councillor Yizhong had not yet returned to court, he was not dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, because Grand Councillor Chen Yizhong had not yet returned to court, he was not sent out.

sentences.zh: 十月，宜中至，始遣之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Yizhong arrived, and only then was he dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Chen Yizhong arrived, and only then was Tianxiang dispatched.

sentences.zh: 朝議方擢呂師孟為兵部尚書，封呂文德和義郡王，欲賴以求好。

translations.literal: The court was just about to promote Lü Shimeng to Minister of War and enfeoff Lü Wende as Prince of the Command of Righteousness, intending to rely on this to seek peace.
translations.idiomatic: The court was about to promote Lü Shimeng to Minister of War and enfeoff Lü Wende as Prince of the Command of Righteousness, hoping to win favor through them.

sentences.zh: 師孟益偃蹇自肆。

translations.literal: Shimeng became all the more arrogant and self-indulgent.
translations.idiomatic: Shimeng grew all the more arrogant and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 天祥陛辭，上疏言：「朝廷姑息牽制之意多，奮發剛斷之義少，乞斬師孟釁鼓，以作將士之氣。」

translations.literal: At his audience on departure Tianxiang submitted a memorial saying: "The court's disposition to conciliate and restrain itself is abundant, but the resolve to rouse and act with firm decisiveness is meager. I beg that Shimeng be executed and his blood smeared on the war drums, to raise the spirit of officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience on departure Tianxiang submitted a memorial: "The court indulges in conciliation and restraint far too much, and resolves to act with bold decisiveness far too little. I beg that Shimeng be executed and his blood smeared on the war drums, to raise the spirit of the officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 且言：「宋懲五季之亂，削藩鎮，建郡邑，一時雖足以矯尾大之弊，然國亦以浸弱。

translations.literal: He also said: "The Song, taking warning from the chaos of the Five Dynasties, abolished military commissions and established prefectures and counties. For a time this indeed remedied the evil of a tail too large to wag, yet the state also gradually weakened.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Taking warning from the chaos of the Five Dynasties, the Song abolished regional military commissions and built up civil administration. For a time this did cure the evil of overmighty provinces, yet the state also grew steadily weaker.

sentences.zh: 故敵至一州則破一州，至一縣則破一縣，中原陸沈，痛悔何及。

translations.literal: Therefore when the enemy reached one prefecture, that prefecture was broken; when they reached one county, that county was broken. The Central Plain sank beneath the waters—what bitter regret could come in time?
translations.idiomatic: So when the enemy reached a prefecture, that prefecture fell; when they reached a county, that county fell. The heartland sank like land lost beneath the flood—what use was bitter regret then?

sentences.zh: 今宜分天下為四鎮，建都督統御於其中。

translations.literal: Now the realm should be divided into four great garrisons, with grand marshals established within them to command overall.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm should be divided into four regional commands, each under a grand marshal with full authority.

sentences.zh: 以廣西益湖南而建閫於長沙；

translations.literal: Adding Guangxi to Hunan and establishing a command headquarters at Changsha;
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi should be added to Hunan, with a command headquarters at Changsha;

sentences.zh: 以廣東益江西而建閫於隆興；

translations.literal: adding Guangdong to Jiangxi and establishing a command headquarters at Longxing;
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong to Jiangxi, with a command headquarters at Longxing;

sentences.zh: 以福建益江東而建閫於番陽；

translations.literal: adding Fujian to Jiangdong and establishing a command headquarters at Poyang;
translations.idiomatic: Fujian to Jiangdong, with a command headquarters at Poyang;

sentences.zh: 以淮西益淮東而建閫於揚州。

translations.literal: adding Huai West to Huai East and establishing a command headquarters at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and Huai West to Huai East, with a command headquarters at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 責長沙取鄂，隆興取蘄、黃，番陽取江東，揚州取兩淮，使其地大力眾，足以抗敵。

translations.literal: Charge Changsha to take E, Longxing to take Qi and Huang, Poyang to take Jiangdong, and Yangzhou to take both Huai regions, so that their territories are broad, their forces numerous, and sufficient to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Charge Changsha to seize Ezhou, Longxing to take Qi and Huang, Poyang to recover Jiangdong, and Yangzhou to recover both banks of the Huai, so that each command would have breadth of territory and strength of numbers enough to resist the enemy.

sentences.zh: 約日齊奮，有進無退，日夜以圖之，彼備多力分，疲於奔命，而吾民之豪傑者又伺間出於其中，如此則敵不難卻也。」

translations.literal: Fix a day to rouse together; advance and never retreat; press the plan day and night. The enemy, with many defenses and divided strength, will weary themselves rushing about, while our people's bold spirits will also watch for openings to sally forth among them—thus the enemy will not be hard to drive back.
translations.idiomatic: Fix a day for all to rise together—advance and never retreat—and press the plan day and night. The enemy, stretched thin across many defenses, would wear themselves out rushing to every alarm, while our own bold spirits would watch for openings to strike from within their lines. In this way the enemy would not be hard to drive back.

sentences.zh: 時議以天祥論闊遠，書奏不報。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion judged Tianxiang's proposals too broad and remote; his memorial was submitted but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion judged Tianxiang's proposals impractically broad; his memorial was submitted but never answered.

sentences.zh: 十月，天祥入平江，大元兵已發金陵入常州矣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Tianxiang entered Pingjiang; Great Yuan troops had already set out from Jinling and entered Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Tianxiang entered Pingjiang; Yuan troops had already marched from Jinling into Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 天祥遣其將朱華、尹玉、麻士龍與張全援常，至虞橋，士龍戰死，朱華以廣軍戰五牧，敗績，玉軍亦敗，爭渡水，挽全軍舟，全軍斷其指，皆溺死，玉以殘兵五百人夜戰，比旦皆沒。

translations.literal: Tianxiang sent his generals Zhu Hua, Yin Yu, and Ma Shilong with Zhang Quan to aid Changzhou. At Yu Bridge Shilong died in battle. Zhu Hua fought at Wumu with Guang troops and was defeated. Yu's army was also defeated; struggling to cross the water, they grabbed hold of Quan's boats; Quan's army cut off their fingers, and all drowned. Yu fought at night with five hundred remnant troops; by dawn all were gone.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang sent his generals Zhu Hua, Yin Yu, and Ma Shilong with Zhang Quan to relieve Changzhou. At Yu Bridge, Shilong was killed in battle. Zhu Hua fought at Wumu with Guang troops and was routed. Yu's army was also defeated; men struggling to cross the water grabbed hold of Quan's boats, and Quan's troops cut off their fingers—every one of them drowned. Yu fought through the night with five hundred remnant soldiers; by dawn all were lost.

sentences.zh: 全不發一矢，走歸。

translations.literal: Quan did not shoot a single arrow and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Quan did not loose a single arrow and fled home.

sentences.zh: 大元兵破常州，入獨松關。

translations.literal: Great Yuan troops broke Changzhou and entered Dusong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan troops broke Changzhou and entered Dusong Pass.

sentences.zh: 宜中、夢炎召天祥，棄平江，守余杭。

translations.literal: Yizhong and Mengyan summoned Tianxiang, abandoned Pingjiang, and defended Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yizhong and Xie Mengyan summoned Tianxiang, abandoned Pingjiang, and fell back to defend Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，除知臨安府。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he was appointed prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year he was appointed prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 未幾，宋降，宜中、世傑皆去。

translations.literal: Before long the Song surrendered; Yizhong and Shijie both departed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Song surrendered; Chen Yizhong and Lu Shijie both departed.

sentences.zh: 仍除天祥樞密使。

translations.literal: Tianxiang was nevertheless appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang was nevertheless appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋除右丞相兼樞密使，使如軍中請和，與大元丞相伯顏抗論皋亭山。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Right Grand Councillor with concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs and sent to the army to sue for peace; at Gaoting Mountain he argued face to face with Bayan, Grand Councillor of the Great Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Right Grand Councillor with concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs and sent to the army to sue for peace; at Gaoting Mountain he argued face to face with Bayan, Grand Councillor of the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 丞相怒拘之，偕左丞相吳堅、右丞相賈餘慶、知樞密院事謝堂、簽書樞密院事家鉉翁、同簽書樞密院事劉岊，北至鎮江。
