translations.literal: The Grand Councillor, in anger, detained him, and together with Left Grand Councillor Wu Jian, Right Grand Councillor Jia Yuqing, Chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs Xie Tang, Secretariat Drafter of the Bureau of Military Affairs Jia Xianweng, and Associate Secretariat Drafter Liu Yi, went north as far as Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan, enraged, detained him and marched north as far as Zhenjiang together with Left Grand Councillor Wu Jian, Right Grand Councillor Jia Yuqing, Chief of the Bureau of Military Affairs Xie Tang, Secretariat Drafter Jia Xianweng, and Associate Secretariat Drafter Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 天祥與其客杜滸十二人，夜亡入真州。

translations.literal: Tianxiang, with his guest Du Yan and eleven others, fled by night into Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang fled by night into Zhen Prefecture with his guest Du Yan and eleven companions.

sentences.zh: 苗再成出迎，喜且泣曰：「兩淮兵足以興復，特二閫小隙，不能合從耳。」

translations.literal: Miao Zaicheng came out to welcome him, joyful and weeping, and said: "The troops of the two Huai regions are enough to restore the dynasty—only a small rift between the two commanders keeps them from joining in alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Zaicheng came out to welcome him, overjoyed and weeping: "The troops of the two Huai regions are enough to restore the dynasty—only a petty quarrel between the two commanders keeps them from joining forces.

sentences.zh: 天祥問：「計將安出？」

translations.literal: Tianxiang asked: "What plan do you propose?
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang asked: "What is your plan?

sentences.zh: 再成曰：「今先約淮西兵趨建康，彼必悉力以捍吾西兵。

translations.literal: Zaicheng said: "Now first arrange for Huai West troops to hurry toward Jiankang—the enemy will surely commit their full strength to block our western force.
translations.idiomatic: Zaicheng said: "First have the Huai West troops march on Jiankang—the enemy will surely commit their full strength to block our western column.

sentences.zh: 指揮東諸將，以通、泰兵攻灣頭，以高郵、寶應、淮安兵攻楊子橋，以揚兵攻瓜步，吾以舟師直搗鎮江，同日大舉。

translations.literal: Direct the eastern generals: with Tong and Tai troops attack Wantou; with Gaoyou, Baoying, and Huai'an troops attack Yangzi Bridge; with Yang troops attack Guabu; I myself with the fleet will strike straight at Zhenjiang—all on the same day in great force.
translations.idiomatic: Then direct the eastern generals: Tong and Tai troops against Wantou, Gaoyou, Baoying, and Huai'an troops against Yangzi Bridge, Yangzhou troops against Guabu—I myself will lead the fleet straight at Zhenjiang. All on the same day, in full force.

sentences.zh: 灣頭、楊子橋皆沿江脆兵，且日夜望我師之至，攻之即下。

translations.literal: Wantou and Yangzi Bridge are both held by weak riverside garrisons that day and night await our army's arrival; attack them and they will fall at once.
translations.idiomatic: Wantou and Yangzi Bridge are both held by weak riverside garrisons that have been waiting day and night for our army; take them and they will fall at once.

sentences.zh: 合攻瓜步之三面，吾自江中一面薄之，雖有智者不能為之謀矣。

translations.literal: Combined attacks on three sides of Guabu, with me pressing from the river on the fourth—even the wisest man could not plan against this.
translations.idiomatic: With combined attacks on three sides of Guabu and me pressing from the river on the fourth, even the wisest commander could devise no counter.

sentences.zh: 瓜步既舉，以東兵入京口，西兵入金陵，要浙歸路，其大帥可坐致也。」

translations.literal: Once Guabu is taken, eastern troops enter Jingkou and western troops enter Jinling, cutting off the Zhejiang line of retreat—their commander-in-chief can be taken sitting down.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guabu falls, eastern troops enter Jingkou and western troops enter Jinling, cutting off the Zhejiang line of retreat—their commander-in-chief can be taken without moving from his seat.

sentences.zh: 天祥大稱善，即以書遺二制置，遣使四齣約結。

translations.literal: Tianxiang greatly praised the plan, immediately sent letters to the two pacification commissioners, and dispatched envoys in four directions to arrange the alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang praised the plan highly, wrote at once to the two pacification commissioners, and sent envoys in four directions to seal the alliance.

sentences.zh: 天祥未至時，揚有脫歸兵言：「密遣一丞相入真州說降矣。」

translations.literal: Before Tianxiang arrived, at Yang there was a soldier who had escaped and returned who said: "A grand councillor has been secretly sent into Zhen Prefecture to urge surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Before Tianxiang arrived, an escaped soldier at Yangzhou reported: "A grand councillor has been secretly sent into Zhen Prefecture to urge surrender.

sentences.zh: 庭芝信之，以為天祥來說降也。

translations.literal: Tingzhi believed it and thought Tianxiang had come to urge surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingzhi believed it and took Tianxiang for a surrender envoy.

sentences.zh: 使再成亟殺之。

translations.literal: He ordered Zaicheng to kill him quickly.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Zaicheng to kill him at once.

sentences.zh: 再成不忍，紿天祥出相城壘，以制司文示之，閉之門外。

translations.literal: Zaicheng could not bear to; he deceived Tianxiang into coming outside the ramparts, showed him the pacification commissioner's order, and shut him outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zaicheng could not bring himself to do it; he tricked Tianxiang outside the ramparts, showed him the pacification commissioner's order, and shut him out.

sentences.zh: 久之，復遣二路分覘天祥，果說降者即殺之。

translations.literal: After a long while he again sent the two route officers to reconnoiter Tianxiang—with orders that if he truly had come to urge surrender, he was to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he sent the two route officers to scout Tianxiang—with orders to kill him if he had truly come to urge surrender.

sentences.zh: 二路分與天祥語，見其忠義，亦不忍殺，以兵二十人道之揚，四鼓抵城下，聞候門者談，制置司下令備文丞相甚急，眾相顧吐舌，乃東入海道，遇兵，伏環堵中得免。

translations.literal: The two route officers spoke with Tianxiang and, seeing his loyalty and righteousness, also could not bear to kill him. They escorted him with twenty soldiers toward Yang; at the fourth watch they reached the foot of the city wall. Hearing the gate guards talk, they learned the pacification commissioner's order to arrest Chancellor Wen was very urgent; the men looked at one another in alarm. They then turned east along the sea route, encountered enemy troops, and escaped by hiding in a ring of walls.
translations.idiomatic: The two route officers spoke with Tianxiang and, seeing his loyalty and righteousness, also could not kill him. Twenty soldiers escorted him toward Yangzhou; at the fourth watch they reached the foot of the wall. Overhearing the gate guards, they learned the pacification commissioner had urgently ordered Wen's arrest; the men exchanged frightened glances. They turned east along the coastal route, ran into enemy troops, and escaped by hiding inside a walled compound.

sentences.zh: 然亦飢莫能起，從樵者乞得余糝羹。

translations.literal: Yet they were so hungry they could not rise; from woodcutters they begged leftover gruel.
translations.idiomatic: They were too hungry even to stand; from woodcutters they begged leftover rice gruel.

sentences.zh: 行入板橋，兵又至，眾走伏叢筱中，兵入索之，執杜滸、金應而去。

translations.literal: As they entered Banqiao, troops came again; the party fled and hid in bamboo thickets. The soldiers entered to search, seized Du Yan and Jin Ying, and took them away.
translations.idiomatic: Near Banqiao they ran into troops again; the party fled and hid in bamboo thickets. Searching soldiers seized Du Yan and Jin Ying and marched them off.

sentences.zh: 虞候張慶矢中目，身被二創，天祥偶不見獲。

translations.literal: Adjutant Zhang Qing was struck in the eye by an arrow and wounded twice on his body; Tianxiang by chance was not captured.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Zhang Qing took an arrow in the eye and two wounds on his body; Tianxiang by chance escaped capture.

sentences.zh: 滸、應解所懷金與卒，獲免，募二樵者以蕢荷天祥至高郵，泛海至溫州。

translations.literal: Yan and Ying gave away the gold hidden on their persons to the soldiers and were spared; they recruited two woodcutters to carry Tianxiang in baskets to Gaoyou and crossed the sea to Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan and Jin Ying bought their freedom with the gold they carried; they hired two woodcutters to carry Tianxiang in baskets to Gaoyou, then crossed the sea to Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 聞益王未立，乃上表勸進，以觀文殿學士、侍讀召至福，拜右丞相。

translations.literal: Hearing that the Prince of Yi had not yet been enthroned, he submitted a memorial urging accession; summoned as Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture and Reader-in-Waiting to Fu, he was appointed Right Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the Prince of Yi had not yet been enthroned, he submitted a memorial urging accession; summoned to Fu as Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture and Reader-in-Waiting, he was appointed Right Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 尋與宜中等議不合。

translations.literal: Soon he found himself at odds with Yizhong and others in council.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell out with Chen Yizhong and others over policy.

sentences.zh: 七月，乃以同都督出江西，遂行，收兵入汀州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was made Co-Director-General and sent out into Jiangxi; he set out at once and gathered troops into Ting Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was made Co-Director-General and sent into Jiangxi; he set out at once and gathered troops at Ting Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十月，遣參謀趙時賞、諮議趙孟溁將一軍取寧都，參贊吳浚將一軍取雩都，劉洙、蕭明哲、陳子敬皆自江西起兵來會。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he sent staff officer Zhao Shishang and adviser Zhao Mengqin to lead one army to take Ningdu; staff officer Wu Jun to lead one army to take Yudu; Liu Zhu, Xiao Mingzhe, and Chen Zijing all raised troops in Jiangxi and came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he sent staff officer Zhao Shishang and adviser Zhao Mengqin with one army to take Ningdu, staff officer Wu Jun with another to take Yudu; Liu Zhu, Xiao Mingzhe, and Chen Zijing all raised troops in Jiangxi and marched to join him.

sentences.zh: 鄒洬以招諭副使聚兵寧都，大元兵攻之，洬兵敗，同起事者劉欽、鞠華叔、顏斯立、顏起岩皆死。

translations.literal: Zou Bing, as Vice Commissioner for Summoning and Reassurance, gathered troops at Ningdu; Great Yuan troops attacked, Bing's army was defeated, and fellow rebels Liu Qin, Ju Huashu, Yan Sili, and Yan Qiyan all died.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Bing, as Vice Commissioner for Summoning and Reassurance, gathered troops at Ningdu; Yuan troops attacked, his army was routed, and fellow rebels Liu Qin, Ju Huashu, Yan Sili, and Yan Qiyan all died.

sentences.zh: 武岡教授羅開禮，起兵復永豐縣，已而兵敗被執，死於獄。

translations.literal: Luo Kaili, instructor at Wugang, raised troops and recovered Yongfeng County; soon his army was defeated, he was seized, and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Kaili, an instructor at Wugang, raised troops and recovered Yongfeng County; soon he was defeated, captured, and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 天祥聞開禮死，制服哭之哀。

translations.literal: When Tianxiang heard of Kaili's death, he put on mourning garments and wept for him in deepest grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianxiang heard of Kaili's death, he put on mourning and wept for him in deepest grief.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年正月，大元兵入汀州，天祥遂移漳州，乞入衛。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, Great Yuan troops entered Ting Prefecture; Tianxiang then shifted to Zhang Prefecture and begged permission to enter and guard the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, Yuan troops entered Ting Prefecture; Tianxiang then shifted to Zhang Prefecture and begged permission to go to court.

sentences.zh: 時賞、孟溁亦提兵歸，獨浚兵不至。

translations.literal: Shishang and Mengqin also led troops back; only Jun's army did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shishang and Zhao Mengqin also led their troops back; only Wu Jun's army failed to arrive.

sentences.zh: 未幾，浚降，來說天祥。

translations.literal: Before long Jun surrendered and came to urge Tianxiang to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wu Jun surrendered and came to urge Tianxiang to do the same.

sentences.zh: 天祥縛浚，縊殺之。

translations.literal: Tianxiang bound Jun and hanged him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang bound Wu Jun and hanged him.

sentences.zh: 四月，入梅州，都統王福、錢漢英跋扈，斬以徇。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he entered Meizhou; commanders Wang Fu and Qian Hanying were overbearing and defiant, and he executed them as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he entered Meizhou; commanders Wang Fu and Qian Hanying had grown overbearing and defiant, and he executed them as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 五月，出江西，入會昌。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he left Jiangxi and entered Huichang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he marched out of Jiangxi into Huichang.

sentences.zh: 六月，入興國縣。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he entered Xingguo County.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he entered Xingguo County.

sentences.zh: 七月，遣參謀張汴、監軍趙時賞、趙孟溁等盛兵薄贛城，鄒洬以贛諸縣兵搗永豐，其副黎貴達以吉諸縣兵攻泰和。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he sent staff officer Zhang Bian, military inspector Zhao Shishang, Zhao Mengqin, and others with a large force to press on Gan City; Zou Bing with the troops of Gan prefectures raided Yongfeng, and his deputy Li Guida with Ji prefecture troops attacked Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he sent staff officer Zhang Bian, military inspector Zhao Shishang, Zhao Mengqin, and others with a strong force against Ganzhou; Zou Bing raided Yongfeng with troops from the Gan prefectures, while his deputy Li Guida attacked Taihe with troops from the Ji prefectures.

sentences.zh: 吉八縣復其半，惟贛不下。

translations.literal: Of Ji's eight counties, half were recovered; only Gan would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Half of Ji's eight counties were recovered; only Ganzhou would not fall.

sentences.zh: 臨洪諸郡，皆送款。

translations.literal: The prefectures around Lin and Hong all submitted pledges of allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures around Lin and Hong all sent pledges of submission.

sentences.zh: 潭趙璠、張虎、張唐、熊桂、劉斗元、吳希奭、陳子全、王夢應起兵邵、永間，復數縣，撫州何時等皆起兵應天祥。

translations.literal: In Tan, Zhao Fan, Zhang Hu, Zhang Tang, Xiong Gui, Liu Douyuan, Wu Xiay, Chen Ziquan, and Wang Mengying raised troops between Shao and Yong and recovered several counties; He Shi of Fuzhou and others all raised troops in response to Tianxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Hunan, Zhao Fan, Zhang Hu, Zhang Tang, Xiong Gui, Liu Douyuan, Wu Xiay, Chen Ziquan, and Wang Mengying raised troops between Shaoyang and Yongzhou and recovered several counties; He Shi of Fuzhou and others all rose in response to Tianxiang.

sentences.zh: 分寧、武寧、建昌三縣豪傑，皆遣人如軍中受約束。

translations.literal: The leading men of Fenning, Wuning, and Jianchang counties all sent men to the army to accept orders.
translations.idiomatic: Leading men from Fenning, Wuning, and Jianchang all sent representatives to his camp to submit to his command.

sentences.zh: 江西宣慰使李恆遣兵援贛州，而自將兵攻天祥於興國。

translations.literal: Li Heng, Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner, sent troops to relieve Ganzhou and personally led troops to attack Tianxiang at Xingguo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Heng, Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner, sent troops to relieve Ganzhou while personally leading an attack on Tianxiang at Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 天祥不意恆兵猝至，乃引兵走，即鄒洬於永豐。

translations.literal: Tianxiang did not expect Heng's troops to arrive so suddenly; he led his army in flight and joined Zou Bing at Yongfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang did not expect Heng's army to strike so suddenly; he retreated and joined Zou Bing at Yongfeng.

sentences.zh: 洬兵先潰，恆窮追天祥方石嶺。

translations.literal: Bing's troops broke first; Heng pursued Tianxiang relentlessly to Fangshi Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Bing's troops broke first; Heng pursued Tianxiang relentlessly to Fangshi Ridge.

sentences.zh: 鞏信拒戰，箭被體，死之。

translations.literal: Gong Xin resisted in battle; arrows covered his body, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Xin stood and fought; arrows covered his body, and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 至空坑，軍士皆潰，天祥妻妾子女皆見執。

translations.literal: At Kongkeng the soldiers all scattered; Tianxiang's wives, concubines, and children were all seized.
translations.idiomatic: At Kongkeng the army scattered; Tianxiang's wives, concubines, and children were all captured.

sentences.zh: 時賞坐肩輿，後兵問謂誰，時賞曰「我姓文」，眾以為天祥，禽之而歸，天祥以此得逸去。

translations.literal: Shishang was riding in a shoulder litter; soldiers coming behind asked who he was. Shishang said, "My surname is Wen." The crowd took him for Tianxiang, seized him, and carried him off; Tianxiang thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shishang was being carried in a litter; pursuing soldiers asked who he was. Shishang said, "My surname is Wen." They took him for Tianxiang, seized him, and marched him off—allowing Tianxiang to escape.

sentences.zh: 孫㮚、彭震龍、張汴死於兵，繆朝宗自縊死。

translations.literal: Sun Sui, Peng Zhenlong, and Zhang Bian died in battle; Miao Chaozong hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sui, Peng Zhenlong, and Zhang Bian died fighting; Miao Chaozong hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 吳文炳、林棟、劉洙皆被執歸隆興。

translations.literal: Wu Wenbing, Lin Dong, and Liu Zhu were all seized and taken back to Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wenbing, Lin Dong, and Liu Zhu were all captured and taken back to Longxing.

sentences.zh: 時賞奮罵不屈，有繫累至者，輒麾去，云：「小小簽廳官耳，執此何為？」

translations.literal: Shishang railed fiercely and would not yield; when bound captives were brought to him, he would wave them away, saying: "A petty secretariat clerk—what is the use of seizing this one?
translations.idiomatic: Shishang railed fiercely and would not yield; when other prisoners were brought before him, he would wave them away: "I'm only a petty secretariat clerk—what use am I to you?

sentences.zh: 由是得脫者甚眾。

translations.literal: Thus very many were able to escape.
translations.idiomatic: In this way many others were able to escape.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，洙頗自辯，時賞叱曰：「死耳，何必然？」

translations.literal: Facing execution, Zhu argued for himself at length; Shishang shouted at him: "We die—that is all. Why be so certain?
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of execution, Liu Zhu pleaded his case at length; Shishang shouted him down: "We die—that is all. Why insist on your innocence?

sentences.zh: 於是棟、文炳、蕭敬夫、蕭燾夫皆不免。

translations.literal: Thereupon Dong, Wenbing, Xiao Jingfu, and Xiao Taofu could not escape death.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Lin Dong, Wu Wenbing, Xiao Jingfu, and Xiao Taofu all died as well.

sentences.zh: 天祥收殘兵奔循州，駐南嶺。

translations.literal: Tianxiang gathered remnant troops and fled to Xun Prefecture, encamping at Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang gathered his remnant troops and fled to Xun Prefecture, encamping at Nanling.

sentences.zh: 黎貴達潛謀降，執而殺之。

translations.literal: Li Guida secretly plotted to surrender; Tianxiang seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guida secretly plotted surrender; Tianxiang seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: 至元十五年三月，進屯麗江浦。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan he advanced and encamped at Lijiang Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan he advanced and encamped at Lijiang Ford.

sentences.zh: 六月，入船澳。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he entered Chuan'ao.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he entered Chuan'ao.

sentences.zh: 益王殂，衛王繼立。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi died; the Prince of Wei succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yi died; the Prince of Wei was enthroned in his place.

sentences.zh: 天祥上表自劾，乞入朝，不許。

translations.literal: Tianxiang submitted a memorial impeaching himself and begged to enter court; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang submitted a memorial of self-reproach and begged to come to court; his request was denied.

sentences.zh: 八月，加天祥少保、信國公。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Tianxiang was promoted to Junior Guardian and enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Faith.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Tianxiang was made Junior Guardian and enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Faith.

sentences.zh: 軍中疫且起，兵士死者數百人。

translations.literal: Plague broke out in the army, and several hundred soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Plague broke out in the army, and several hundred soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 天祥惟一子，與其母皆死。

translations.literal: Tianxiang's only son, together with his mother, both died.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang's only son and the boy's mother both died.

sentences.zh: 十一月，進屯潮陽縣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he advanced and encamped at Chaoyang County.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he advanced and encamped at Chaoyang County.

sentences.zh: 潮州盜陳懿、劉興數叛附，為潮人害。

translations.literal: The bandits of Chaozhou, Chen Yi and Liu Xing, repeatedly switched sides, and were a calamity to the people of Chao.
translations.idiomatic: The Chaozhou bandits Chen Yi and Liu Xing repeatedly changed sides, plaguing the people of the region.

sentences.zh: 天祥攻走懿，執興誅之。

translations.literal: Tianxiang attacked and drove off Yi, seized Xing, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang attacked and drove off Chen Yi, seized Liu Xing, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，趨南嶺，鄒洬、劉子俊又自江西起兵來，再攻懿黨，懿乃潛道元帥張弘范兵濟潮陽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he hurried to Nanling; Zou Bing and Liu Zijun again raised troops in Jiangxi and came; attacking Yi's faction once more, Yi then secretly guided Marshal Zhang Hongfan's troops across to Chaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he hurried to Nanling; Zou Bing and Liu Zijun again raised troops in Jiangxi and joined him. Attacking Chen Yi's faction once more, Yi secretly guided Marshal Zhang Hongfan's troops into Chaoyang.

sentences.zh: 天祥方飯五坡嶺，張弘范兵突至，眾不及戰，皆頓首伏草莽。

translations.literal: Tianxiang was just taking a meal at Wupo Ridge when Zhang Hongfan's troops burst upon him; the men had no time to fight and all bowed their heads prostrate in the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang was taking a meal at Wupo Ridge when Zhang Hongfan's troops burst upon him; his men had no time to fight and all prostrated themselves in the brush.

sentences.zh: 天祥倉皇出走，千戶王惟義前執之。

translations.literal: Tianxiang fled in confusion; Thousand-Household Wang Weiyi rushed forward and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang fled in panic; Thousand-Household Wang Weiyi rushed forward and seized him.

sentences.zh: 天祥吞腦子，不死。

translations.literal: Tianxiang swallowed poison and did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang swallowed poison but did not die.

sentences.zh: 鄒洬自頸，眾扶入南嶺死。

translations.literal: Zou Bing cut his own throat; the crowd supported him into Nanling, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Bing cut his own throat; his companions helped him into Nanling, where he died.

sentences.zh: 官屬士卒得脫空坑者，至是劉子俊、陳龍復、蕭明哲、蕭資皆死，杜滸被執，以憂死。

translations.literal: Among officials, followers, and soldiers who had escaped at Kongkeng, at this time Liu Zijun, Chen Longfu, Xiao Mingzhe, and Xiao Zi all died; Du Yan was seized and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Of the officials, followers, and soldiers who had escaped at Kongkeng, Liu Zijun, Chen Longfu, Xiao Mingzhe, and Xiao Zi all died here; Du Yan was captured and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 惟趙孟溁遁，張唐、熊桂、吳希奭、陳子全兵敗被獲，俱死焉。

translations.literal: Only Zhao Mengqin escaped; Zhang Tang, Xiong Gui, Wu Xiay, and Chen Ziquan were defeated in battle, seized, and all died.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhao Mengqin escaped; Zhang Tang, Xiong Gui, Wu Xiay, and Chen Ziquan were defeated, captured, and all perished.

sentences.zh: 唐，廣漢張栻後也。

translations.literal: Tang was a descendant of Zhang Shi of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: Tang was a descendant of Zhang Shi of Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 天祥至潮陽，見弘范，左右命之拜，不拜，弘范遂以客禮見之，與俱入厓山，使為書招張世傑。

translations.literal: Tianxiang reached Chaoyang and met Hongfan; those at his side ordered him to bow, but he would not; Hongfan then received him with guest ceremony, went with him into Yashan, and had him write a letter to summon Zhang Shijie.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianxiang reached Chaoyang he met Zhang Hongfan; attendants ordered him to bow, but he refused; Hongfan then received him as a guest, accompanied him to Yashan, and asked him to write summoning Zhang Shijie.

sentences.zh: 天祥曰：「吾不能捍父母，乃教人叛父母，可乎？」

translations.literal: Tianxiang said: "I could not defend my parents—how could I teach others to betray their parents?"
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang said, "I could not defend my sovereign—how could I urge another to betray his?"

sentences.zh: 索之固，乃書所過《零丁洋詩》與之。

translations.literal: When pressed insistently, he wrote out for him the poem he had composed at Lingding Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed repeatedly, he wrote out for him the poem he had composed at Lingding Sea.

sentences.zh: 其末有云：「人生自古誰無死，留取丹心照汗青。」

translations.literal: Its closing lines read: "Since antiquity, who has escaped death? Let a loyal heart shine through the annals."
translations.idiomatic: Its closing lines read: "Since antiquity, who escapes death? Let a loyal heart shine in the annals."

sentences.zh: 弘范笑而置之。

translations.literal: Hongfan smiled and set it aside.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan smiled and set it aside.

sentences.zh: 厓山破，軍中置酒大會，弘范曰：「國亡，丞相忠孝盡矣，能改心以事宋者事皇上，將不失為宰相也。」

translations.literal: When Yashan fell, the army set out wine for a great gathering; Hongfan said: "The state is lost and the Chancellor's loyalty and filial piety are complete; if you can change your heart and serve the Song as you would serve Our Emperor, you will not lose the post of chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: When Yashan fell, the army held a great feast; Hongfan said, "The state is lost and you have done all loyalty and filial piety require; if you will turn your heart and serve the emperor as you served the Song, you may still be chief minister."

sentences.zh: 天祥泫然出涕，曰：「國亡不能救，為人臣者死有餘罪，況敢逃其死而二其心乎。」

translations.literal: Tianxiang wept tears streaming down and said: "The state is lost and I could not save it; as a minister death leaves me still in debt—how much less could I flee death and serve two masters?"
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang wept and said, "The state is lost and I could not save it; as a minister I deserve death—how could I flee it and serve two masters?"

sentences.zh: 弘范義之，遣使護送天祥至京師。

translations.literal: Hongfan admired his integrity and sent an envoy to escort Tianxiang to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan admired his integrity and sent him under escort to the capital.

sentences.zh: 天祥在道，不食八日，不死，即復食。

translations.literal: On the road Tianxiang ate nothing for eight days yet did not die, and then ate again.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey Tianxiang fasted eight days without dying, then ate again.

sentences.zh: 至燕，館人供張甚盛，天祥不寢處，坐達旦。

translations.literal: Reaching Yan, the host's provisions were very lavish; Tianxiang would not lie down but sat until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: At Yan the lodging was lavishly furnished; Tianxiang would not sleep but sat until dawn.

sentences.zh: 遂移兵馬司，設卒以守之。

translations.literal: He was then moved to the Bureau of Horses and Mules, and guards were set to watch him.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the military stables compound and placed under guard.

sentences.zh: 時世祖皇帝多求才南官，王積翁言：「南人無如天祥者。」

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Shizu sought talent widely among southern officials; Wang Jinweng said: "Among southerners there is none like Tianxiang."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu was recruiting southern talent; Wang Jinweng said, "Among southerners there is no one like Tianxiang."

sentences.zh: 遂遣積翁諭旨，天祥曰：「國亡，吾分一死矣。

translations.literal: Jinweng was then sent to convey the imperial will; Tianxiang said: "The state is lost—I am owed but one death.
translations.idiomatic: Jinweng was sent with the emperor's message; Tianxiang replied, "The state is lost—I owe it but one death.

sentences.zh: 儻緣寬假，得以黃冠歸故鄉，他日以方外備顧問，可也。

translations.literal: If by grace of pardon I may return home in Daoist garb, later to serve as an outside adviser, that would be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: If I am pardoned to return home as a Daoist priest and later serve as an outside adviser, that I could accept.

sentences.zh: 若遽官之，非直亡國之大夫不可與圖存，舉其平生而盡棄之，將焉用我？」

translations.literal: If I am hurried into office, not only may a minister of a fallen state not plot survival—my whole life's conduct would be cast away; of what use would I be?"
translations.idiomatic: If I am made an official at once, not only may a minister of a fallen state not plot restoration—my whole life would be thrown away; what use would you have for me?"

sentences.zh: 積翁欲合宋官謝昌元等十人請釋天祥為道士，留夢炎不可，曰「天祥出，復號召江南，置吾十人於何地！」

translations.literal: Jinweng wished to join ten Song officials including Xie Changyuan in asking that Tianxiang be released as a Daoist priest; Liu Mengyan objected, saying: "If Tianxiang is released, he will again rally the south—where will that leave the ten of us!"
translations.idiomatic: Jinweng wanted Xie Changyuan and nine other Song officials to join in asking that Tianxiang be released as a priest; Liu Mengyan objected, "If Tianxiang goes free he will rally the south again—what becomes of us ten?"

sentences.zh: 事遂已。

translations.literal: The matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 天祥在燕凡三年，上知天祥終不屈也，與宰相議釋之，有以天祥起兵江西事為言者，不果釋。

translations.literal: Tianxiang was in Yan altogether three years; the emperor knew he would never yield and discussed releasing him with the chief minister, but someone cited Tianxiang's raising troops in Jiangxi, and he was not released.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang spent three years in Yan; the emperor knew he would never submit and discussed releasing him with his ministers, but someone cited his uprising in Jiangxi, and release was denied.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年，有閩僧言土星犯帝坐，疑有變。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan a Fujian monk said Saturn was trespassing on the imperial seat and suspected trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan a Fujian monk reported Saturn trespassing on the imperial seat and foretold unrest.

sentences.zh: 未幾，中山有狂人自稱「宋主」，有兵千人，欲取文丞相。

translations.literal: Before long in Zhongshan a madman called himself "Lord of Song," with a thousand troops, intending to seize Chancellor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon in Zhongshan a madman proclaimed himself "Lord of Song" with a thousand men, intending to seize Chancellor Wen.

sentences.zh: 京城亦有匿名書，言某日燒蓑城葦，率兩翼兵為亂，丞相可無憂者。

translations.literal: In the capital too there was an anonymous letter saying that on a certain day the reed matting on the walls would be burned and the two wings of troops would rise in revolt—the Chancellor need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: An anonymous letter in the capital warned that on a set day the city reeds would be burned and troops would rebel—the Chancellor was not to be spared.

sentences.zh: 時盜新殺左丞相阿合馬，命撤城葦，遷瀛國公及宋宗室開平，疑丞相者天祥也。

translations.literal: At that time an assassin had just killed Left Chief Councilor Ahmad; the order went out to remove the wall reeds, move the Duke of Ying and the Song imperial clan to Kaiping, and the suspected Chancellor was Tianxiang.
translations.idiomatic: An assassin had just killed Left Chief Councilor Ahmad; the court ordered the wall reeds removed, the Duke of Ying and the Song imperial clan moved to Kaiping, and suspected the Chancellor meant Tianxiang.

sentences.zh: 召入諭之曰：「汝何願？」

translations.literal: He was summoned in and told: "What is your wish?"
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and asked, "What is your wish?"

sentences.zh: 天祥對曰：「天祥受宋恩，為宰相，安事二姓？

translations.literal: Tianxiang replied: "Tianxiang received Song's grace and served as chief minister—how could I serve two dynasties?
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang answered, "I received the Song's grace and served as chief minister—how could I serve two dynasties?

sentences.zh: 願賜之一死足矣。」

translations.literal: I ask only to be granted death—that is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Grant me death—that is all I ask."

sentences.zh: 然猶不忍，遽麾之退。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor still could not bear it and abruptly waved him away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still could not bear it and waved him away.

sentences.zh: 言者力贊從天祥之請，從之。

translations.literal: Those who spoke strongly urged acceding to Tianxiang's request, and it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers urged granting his request, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄有詔使止之，天祥死矣。

translations.literal: Soon an edict messenger came to stop it—but Tianxiang was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: An edict arrived to stay the execution—but Tianxiang was already dead.

sentences.zh: 天祥臨刑殊從容，謂吏卒曰：「吾事畢矣。」

translations.literal: Facing execution Tianxiang was wholly composed and said to the clerks and guards: "My task is finished."
translations.idiomatic: At the block Tianxiang was wholly composed and told the guards, "My work is done."

sentences.zh: 南鄉拜而死。

translations.literal: He bowed toward the south and died.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed toward the south and died.

sentences.zh: 數日，其妻歐陽氏收其屍，面如生，年四十七。

translations.literal: Several days later his wife Lady Ouyang collected his body; his face was as in life; he was forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Days later his wife Lady Ouyang claimed his body; his face looked as in life; he was forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 其衣帶中有贊曰：「孔曰成仁，孟曰取義，惟其義盡，所以仁至。

translations.literal: In his belt was an inscription reading: "Confucius spoke of realizing humanity; Mencius spoke of taking righteousness; only when righteousness is exhausted does humanity reach its fullness.
translations.idiomatic: In his belt was an inscription: "Confucius taught humanity fulfilled in death; Mencius taught taking righteousness; only when righteousness is complete is humanity fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 讀聖賢書，所學何事，而今而後，庶幾無愧。」

translations.literal: What did I study in the books of sages? From this day forward, I may be without shame."
translations.idiomatic: What did I study in the sages' books? From this day on, I may stand without shame."

sentences.zh: 論曰：自古志士，欲信大義於天下者，不以成敗利鈍動其心，君子命之曰「仁」，以其合天理之正，即人心之安爾。

translations.literal: The historian remarks: From antiquity, men of resolve who wished to make great principle trusted throughout the world have not let success or failure, gain or loss move their hearts; the gentleman names this "humanity," because it accords with Heaven's right principle and gives peace to the human heart.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Men of resolve who would uphold great principle in the world have never let success or failure sway them; the gentleman calls this humanity, for it accords with Heaven's right and the peace of the human heart.

sentences.zh: 商之衰，周有代德，盟津之師不期而會者八百國。

translations.literal: When Shang declined, Zhou had the virtue to replace it; at the Meng Ford eight hundred states assembled without prior appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang declined, Zhou possessed the virtue to succeed it; at the Meng Ford eight hundred states gathered unbidden.

sentences.zh: 伯夷、叔齊以兩男子欲扣馬而止之，三尺童子知其不可。

translations.literal: Bo Yi and Shu Qi, two men, wished to seize the horses and stop the army—even a child three feet tall knew it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Yi and Shu Qi, two men alone, tried to seize the horses and halt the army—even a child knew it was futile.

sentences.zh: 他日，孔子賢之，則曰：「求仁而得仁。」

translations.literal: Later Confucius honored them and said: "They sought humanity and obtained humanity."
translations.idiomatic: Later Confucius praised them, saying, "They sought humanity and found it."

sentences.zh: 宋至德祐亡矣，文天祥往來兵間，初欲以口舌存之，事既無成，奉兩孱王崎嶇嶺海，以圖興復，兵敗身執。

translations.literal: When Song reached its end at Deyou, Wen Tianxiang moved among the armies; at first he hoped to preserve it by words alone; when that failed he escorted two feeble sovereigns through rugged mountains and seas to plan restoration; defeated in battle, he was taken prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: When Song fell at Deyou, Wen Tianxiang moved among the armies; first he hoped to save it by persuasion alone; when that failed he escorted two feeble emperors through mountains and seas to plan restoration; defeated, he was captured.

sentences.zh: 我世祖皇帝以天地有容之量，既壯其節，又惜其才，留之數年，如虎兕在柙，百計馴之，終不可得。

translations.literal: Our Emperor Shizu, with the forbearance of Heaven and Earth, admired his integrity and prized his talent, kept him several years like a tiger or rhinoceros in a cage, tried every means to tame him, and in the end could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu, with Heaven and Earth's magnanimity, admired his integrity and prized his talent, kept him for years as a tiger in a cage, tried every means to tame him, and could not.

sentences.zh: 觀其從容伏質，就死如歸，是其所欲有甚於生者，可不謂之「仁」哉。

translations.literal: Observing how composed he was in submitting to execution, going to death as if returning home—what he desired was greater than life itself; can this not be called "humanity"?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how calmly he faced the block, going to death as if going home—what he desired was greater than life; can this not be called humanity?

sentences.zh: 宋三百餘年，取士之科，莫盛於進士，進士莫盛於倫魁。

translations.literal: In Song's more than three hundred years, no method of selecting scholars was greater than the jinshi, and among jinshi none was greater than the top-ranked graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's three centuries, no path to office was greater than the jinshi, and among jinshi none greater than the top-ranked graduate.

sentences.zh: 自天祥死，世之好為高論者，謂科目不足以得偉人，豈其然乎！

translations.literal: Since Tianxiang's death, those in the world fond of lofty talk have said the examination system cannot produce great men—is it really so?
translations.idiomatic: Since Tianxiang's death, those fond of lofty talk have said examinations cannot produce great men—is that really so?
